body:
## Description

This PR parallelizes open-loop evaluation in `autoware_planning_data_analyzer` and ports the implementation onto the current `autowarefoundation/autoware_tools` `main` base.

Included in this PR:

- parallel trajectory evaluation with worker threads for open-loop metrics
- parallel phase split for base metrics and extended comfort / synthetic EPDMS horizon evaluation
- preservation of bag-output equivalence by restoring merge-based final bag generation

The bag finalization path keeps the final output behavior aligned with the previous sequential implementation:

- intermediate bag -> analyzer temp bag -> merged final bag
- no build artifacts are included in this PR

## How was this PR tested?

 ran the full offline pipeline and compared the artifact created before the change this time with the current output:

Validation results from the full pipeline:

- output bag size matched: `56G` vs `56G`
- EPDMS-related aggregate values matched exactly between reference and rerun

Observed analyzer runtime from the successful rerun:

- total analyzer runtime: about `1431.82 s` (`23m 51.8s`)
- open-loop evaluation core: about `1211.38 s` (`20m 11.4s`)
- parallel phase 1: about `527.44 s`
- parallel phase 2: about `611.36 s`

author: ryanklee
body:
## Summary

- `scripts/rebuild-service.sh` used to silently `echo "$CURRENT_SHA" > "$SHA_FILE"` whenever the target repo was on a feature branch instead of `main`, masking deploy failures forever.
- Fix: do NOT update `SHA_FILE` on deploy skip — keep the pending advancement visible so the next cycle re-flags it. Also send a throttled `ntfy` (one per distinct `origin/main` SHA) so the operator notices.
- Does NOT auto-deploy; auto-advancing a feature branch would clobber the operator's work.

## Motivation

Delta's PR #702 merged to main at 20:46 while alpha was on a feature branch. `rebuild-service.sh` silently no-op'd on every invocation, leaving the running reverie daemon 3+ hours stale. The only recovery was a manual force-merge of alpha to `origin/main`. This closes the silent-failure hole so the operator always knows when a pending deploy is blocked on a rebase.

Companion to FU-6 (PR #703), which addressed the compiled-binary path (logos/imagination) via an isolated scratch worktree. That approach doesn't apply here because systemd units point `ExecStart` at alpha's worktree directly — Python services are interpreter-loaded, so the only way to pick up new code is to actually advance the ref the service reads from.

## Test plan

- [x] Off-main smoke test: faked `last-voice-sha`, invoked script against alpha (on fu-6b branch), verified:
  - `SHA_FILE` NOT updated (stays stale)
  - `last-notified-voice-sha` written to `$CURRENT_SHA`
  - journalctl logs "repo not on main … deploy skipped; SHA_FILE NOT updated"
- [x] Throttle test: second invocation with same state left `last-notified-voice-sha` unchanged and did not emit a duplicate `ntfy`
- [x] State cleanup: restored `last-voice-sha` from backup, deleted `last-notified-voice-sha`
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Merge; next real timer firing against an off-main alpha surfaces the fix live

## Out of scope

- Auto-rebase or auto-ff on "HEAD is ancestor of origin/main" — safer but still clobbers. Would require operator confirmation protocol.
- Moving systemd units off alpha's worktree to a dedicated deploy worktree — architectural change that also touches the three-worktree-slot discipline. Better as a standalone design discussion.

author: rikutokanzaki
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces four runtime modes (`dynamic`, `static`, `standalone`, `rotate`) and aligns the full stack behavior (OpenResty, Paramiko, Launcher, install/uninstall flow) with mode-aware operation. It also reorganizes compose files by mode and updates documentation to reflect the new setup and configuration model.

## What Changed
1. Added mode-based operation across the system
- Implemented support for `dynamic`, `static`, `standalone`, and `rotate` modes.
- Added rotate logic to cycle modes on a configurable interval.
- Standardized mode propagation between dispatcher components and launcher control paths.

2. Reorganized Docker Compose profiles
- Moved previous top-level compose profiles into mode-scoped directories.
- Added dedicated profile sets for:
  - `dynamic` (`standard/http/ssh`)
  - `static` (`standard/http/ssh`)
  - `rotate` (`standard/http/ssh`)
  - `standalone` (`cowrie/heralding/h0neytr4p`)

3. Enhanced installer flow
- Added interactive selection for deployment mode and profile.
- Persisted selected values into environment/config metadata.
- Improved startup behavior to stop non-required honeypot services where applicable.

4. Enhanced uninstaller flow
- Added support for uninstalling based on previously selected mode/profile.
- Reads install metadata to prefill defaults and improve consistency.
- Keeps backup/export behavior aligned with selected deployment layout.

5. Updated dispatcher and launcher behavior
- OpenResty: added mode sync/init handling, mode fallback logging, and mode-aware routing decisions.
- Paramiko: added centralized mode manager and mode-aware SSH handling/logging.
- Launcher: added mode application endpoint(s) and mode-based persistent/timeout behavior.

6. Documentation updates
- Updated setup/configuration docs for new mode model.
- Added/clarified env vars such as:
  - `DISPATCHER_MODE`
  - `ROTATE_INTERVAL`
  - `DISPATCHER_HTTP_TARGET`
  - `SESSION_TIMEOUT`

## Why
- Enable flexible operation patterns (resource-efficient, always-on, single-honeypot, and rotating behavior) without changing code between environments.
- Improve operational clarity and reproducibility by making mode/profile explicit at install/uninstall time.
- Keep runtime behavior and documentation consistent with actual deployment structure.

## Validation Checklist
1. Install flow supports selecting each mode and corresponding profile.
2. Selected mode/profile is persisted and reused by uninstall flow.
3. Dynamic mode only starts services on demand.
4. Static mode keeps profile services running persistently.
5. Rotate mode transitions according to `ROTATE_INTERVAL`.
6. Standalone mode routes traffic to the configured standalone target.
7. Uninstall works correctly for each mode/profile combination.

## Breaking Changes / Migration Notes
- Compose file paths have changed due to mode-based directory reorganization.
- Existing scripts or CI jobs referencing old compose paths must be updated.

## Summary

Closes #85.

- Adds content-addressed response caching so unchanged task executions replay from cache instead of hitting the agent API. Cache key is a SHA-256 hash of execution-affecting inputs (prompt, model, runner type, skill content hash, timeout, allowed dirs) — scoring/report config is excluded so judging always runs fresh.

## Summary

- Fix a data race detected by ThreadSanitizer during `MessageBroker` shutdown: the implicit destructor ordering destroyed ZMQ sockets before the `zmq_context_` (which owns the IO thread), leaving a window where the IO thread processes freed metadata.
- `Stop()` now explicitly closes all ZMQ sockets and terminates the context (joining the IO thread) before returning.
- Switch two tests (`DeadNodeIsNotBroadcastViaGossip`, `DeferredReplySurvivesNodeConnectionLossAndReconnection`) to dynamic capture-socket ports and add explicit `capture_ctx.close()` calls, preventing port conflicts and ensuring the capture IO thread is joined.

author: yanhu007
body:
Fixes #125

## Problem

Unicode has two visually identical mu/micro characters:
- **U+00B5** `µ` (MICRO SIGN) — used in the SI prefix table
- **U+03BC** `μ` (GREEK SMALL LETTER MU) — commonly typed via keyboard

`ParseSI` only recognizes U+00B5, so `ParseSI("2.5 μF")` with Greek mu returns `(2.5, "μF", nil)` instead of `(2.5e-6, "F", nil)`.

## Fix

Add U+03BC as an alias in both:
1. The reverse prefix lookup table (`revSIPrefixTable`)
2. The parsing regex character class

```go
ParseSI("2.5 µF") // U+00B5 → (2.5e-6, "F", nil) ✅ (already worked)
ParseSI("2.5 μF") // U+03BC → (2.5e-6, "F", nil) ✅ (now works)
```

All existing tests pass.

author: jarvisniels
body:
## Summary

Fixes the **bad request** error reported in issue #107 for `Invoke-CPCPowerOn` and `Invoke-CPCPowerOff`.

## Root Cause

`Get-CloudPC -Name $Name` returns a **PowerShell array** (even when a single Cloud PC matches), not a scalar object. The original code used `$CloudPC.id` directly in string interpolation — when the array contains even one item, PowerShell's array-member enumeration produces the ID correctly on some builds but can silently produce a space-joined string or empty value on others, causing the Graph API to receive a malformed URL (e.g. `cloudPCs//powerOn` or `cloudPCs/id1 id2/powerOn`).

The same root cause was fixed for `Invoke-CPCChangeUserAccountType` in PR #106. This PR applies the identical fix to the two power-management functions.

## Changes

### `Invoke-CPCPowerOn.ps1`
- Wrap `Get-CloudPC` result in `@()` and check `.Count -eq 0` (handles both `$null` and empty array)
- Take `@($CloudPC)[0]` to guarantee a scalar before reading `.id`
- Add `-CloudPCId` parameter set for direct ID invocation (avoids the lookup entirely)
- Use named `$targetId` / `$targetName` variables for clarity

### `Invoke-CPCPowerOff.ps1`
- Same changes as above

## Testing



## References
- Fixes #107
- Same pattern applied in #106 (Invoke-CPCChangeUserAccountType)
- Graph API: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/cloudpc-poweron
- Graph API: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/cloudpc-poweroff

> **Note:** `PSCloudPC.psd1` is intentionally not modified — manifest updates are handled by the module owner.

## Requirements
Closes #1026

# PR: Project Foundation & Scaffolding for Executive Reporting Dashboard

## Summary

Implements the complete project scaffolding for the Executive Reporting Dashboard — a single-page Blazor Server (.NET 8) application that renders project milestones, shipping status, and monthly execution progress at a fixed 1920×1080 viewport for PowerPoint screenshot capture. This PR establishes the directory structure, .csproj configuration, C# data models, Blazor host infrastructure (App.razor, _Host.cshtml, EmptyLayout), Program.cs with DI registration, _Imports.razor, launchSettings.json, .gitignore, and a CSS stub with all design-system custom properties. No runtime UI rendering is included — this is the foundation that subsequent PRs (data service, dashboard page, heatmap grid) build upon.

**Parent Issue:** #1013  
**Task ID:** T1

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ReportingDashboard/ReportingDashboard/` directory contains the full folder structure: `Pages/`, `Layout/`, `Models/`, `Services/`, `wwwroot/css/`, `wwwroot/data/`, `Properties/`
- [ ] `.gitignore` excludes `bin/`, `obj/`, `publish/`, user secrets, and `.vs/` artifacts
- [ ] `ReportingDashboard.csproj` targets `net8.0` with `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` and `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`, and declares **zero** third-party NuGet package references
- [ ] `Models/DashboardConfig.cs` defines four `record` types (`DashboardConfig`, `Milestone`, `MilestoneEvent`, `HeatmapRow`) with default values on all properties and `[JsonPropertyName]` attributes where needed
- [ ] `Layout/EmptyLayout.razor` inherits `LayoutComponentBase` and renders only `@Body` — no wrapper divs, nav, or sidebar
- [ ] `_Imports.razor` includes `@using` directives for `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Routing`, `ReportingDashboard`, `ReportingDashboard.Models`, `ReportingDashboard.Layout`
- [ ] `Program.cs` registers `AddRazorPages()`, `AddServerSideBlazor()`, `AddSingleton<DashboardDataService>()`, configures `UseStaticFiles()`, `MapBlazorHub()`, and `MapFallbackToPage("/_Host")`
- [ ] `App.razor` defines the Blazor `<Router>` with `<RouteView DefaultLayout="@typeof(EmptyLayout)" />` and a `<NotFound>` fallback
- [ ] `Pages/_Host.cshtml` is a valid Blazor Server host page referencing `/css/dashboard.css` and rendering `<component type="typeof(App)" render-mode="ServerPrerendered" />`
- [ ] `Properties/launchSettings.json` configures HTTPS on port 5001 and HTTP on port 5000
- [ ] `wwwroot/css/dashboard.css` contains a `:root` block with all color tokens from the design spec (shipped green, progress blue, carryover amber, blocker red, page bg, text colors, border colors, current-month highlight)
- [ ] `wwwroot/data/` directory exists (empty or with placeholder) ready for `data.json` in a subsequent PR
- [ ] `dotnet restore` completes with zero errors
- [ ] `dotnet build` compiles with zero errors and zero warnings

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Directory structure, .gitignore, and .csproj

Create the `ReportingDashboard/ReportingDashboard/` project directory with all subdirectories (`Pages/`, `Layout/`, `Models/`, `Services/`, `wwwroot/css/`, `wwwroot/data/`, `Properties/`). Add a `.gitignore` covering standard .NET artifacts (`bin/`, `obj/`, `publish/`, `*.user`, `.vs/`, `*.suo`, `appsettings.*.json` user overrides). Create `ReportingDashboard.csproj` with `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`, targeting `net8.0`, nullable enabled, implicit usings enabled, and zero NuGet references. Verify with `dotnet restore`.

**Produces:** Empty buildable project skeleton.

### Step 2: C# data models and service stub

Create `Models/DashboardConfig.cs` with four `record` types:
- `DashboardConfig` — `Title`, `Subtitle`, `BacklogLink`, `CurrentMonth` (strings), `Months` (List\<string\>), `Milestones` (List\<Milestone\>), `HeatmapRows` (List\<HeatmapRow\>), all with default values.
- `Milestone` — `Label`, `Description`, `Color` (strings), `Events` (List\<MilestoneEvent\>).
- `MilestoneEvent` — `Date`, `Type`, `Label` (strings).
- `HeatmapRow` — `Category`, `Label` (strings, `Label` with `[JsonPropertyName("label")]`), `Items` (Dictionary\<string, List\<string\>\>).

author: ryanklee
body:
## Summary

Composes on top of delta PR #702 (option a — `start_at_end=True`) with option b — `cursor_path` persistence for daemons where missing an impingement would be a correctness bug.

- **#702 fixed reverie** — the visual pipeline's 5–15 min startup stall is gone via skip-on-restart. Correct for reverie (stale impingements cannot meaningfully modulate the next visual tick).
- **This PR covers the stateful consumers** — daimonion affordance loop, daimonion CPAL loop, fortress governance loop. These need crash-resume semantics: a missed impingement corrupts Thompson sampling posteriors / drops a session lifecycle transition / drops a governance event.

## Mechanism

`ImpingementConsumer` now supports three bootstrap modes that compose cleanly:

| Mode | Kwarg | Behavior | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy | (default) | `cursor=0`, read from beginning | tests, stateless callers |
| Skip-on-restart | `start_at_end=True` | bootstrap cursor to end-of-file, no persistence | reverie (delta #702) |
| Persisted cursor | `cursor_path=<Path>` | seek-to-end on first start, resume from saved cursor on subsequent starts, atomic persist on each advance | **daimonion ×2, fortress** (this PR) |

`cursor_path` takes precedence over `start_at_end` because its bootstrap rule (seek-to-end when cursor file is missing) is strictly stronger than delta's unconditional seek-to-end.

### cursor_path bootstrap rules

- Cursor file present + valid integer → resume from saved cursor.
- Cursor file missing → seek to current end-of-file, persist cursor. First-ever startup skips backlog.
- Cursor file corrupt / negative → log warning, seek to end.
- Each `read_new()` advance atomically persists the new cursor via tmp + rename.
- File shrinkage (rotation, truncation) → reset cursor to new length, log warning, return empty from that call.
- Cursor write failures log and proceed without crashing `read_new`.

## Callers wired

- **fortress** `FortressDaemon` — `~/.cache/hapax/impingement-cursor-fortress.txt`
- **daimonion affordance loop** — `~/.cache/hapax/impingement-cursor-daimonion-affordance.txt`
- **daimonion CPAL loop** — `~/.cache/hapax/impingement-cursor-daimonion-cpal.txt`

Reverie is unchanged — delta's `start_at_end=True` is the right call there.

Apperception's `consume_perception_impingements` helper is a stateless per-call reader with caller-managed cursor; doesn't fit either pattern. Unchanged.

## Test isolation (important)

`FortressDaemon` and the daimonion loops take `impingement_cursor_path` as an `__init__` parameter that defaults to `None`. The production entrypoints (`main()` in fortress, the loop creation in the running daimonion) wire the concrete path; tests that construct these without arguments stay on the legacy (cursor=None) path and do not touch `~/.cache/hapax` state.

**Verified: 887 tests pass, zero `impingement-cursor-*.txt` files land in `~/.cache/hapax` during the run.**

## Test coverage

`TestCursorPersistence` — 10 new cases on top of delta's 4 `start_at_end` cases and the 7 original legacy cases (34 total, all passing):

- `first_startup_seeks_to_end_and_skips_backlog`
- `second_startup_resumes_from_persisted_cursor`
- `cursor_persisted_after_read_new_advance`
- `corrupt_cursor_file_falls_back_to_end_of_file`
- `negative_cursor_in_file_falls_back_to_end_of_file`
- `file_shrinkage_resets_cursor_and_returns_empty`
- `cursor_parent_directory_created_on_demand`
- `cursor_path_takes_precedence_over_start_at_end`
- `cursor_write_failure_does_not_crash_read_new`
- `missing_impingement_file_bootstrap`

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_impingement_consumer.py tests/test_reverie_daemon.py tests/test_apperception_impingement_consumer.py tests/fortress/test_main.py -q` → 34 passing
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/ -k "impingement or reverie or fortress or apperception or consumer" --ignore=tests/hapax_daimonion -q` → 887 pass, 11 skipped
- [x] `uv run ruff check` + `ruff format` — clean
- [x] `uv run pyright` on all modified files — 0 errors
- [x] `ls ~/.cache/hapax/impingement-cursor-*.txt` after full test run — none (test isolation verified)
- [ ] Post-merge: `systemctl --user restart hapax-daimonion hapax-fortress` — confirm cursor files land in `~/.cache/hapax/` and stay stable across a second restart

## Convergence notes (logged to `~/.cache/hapax/relay/convergence.log`)

- COMPLEMENTARY with delta #702: same F6 root cause, different durability tier per consumer requirement. Composition pattern — keep delta's `start_at_end` semantics as-is, add `cursor_path` as a strictly-stronger opt-in.

body:
## Summary

Add a new policy that checks whether GitHub's secret scanning feature is enabled on repositories.

## Motivation

As noted in #363, GitHub now offers secret scanning alerts for all public repos, but it must be explicitly enabled. This is exactly the kind of security feature that organizations want to enforce across all their repositories via policy — a natural fit for Allstar.

## Implementation

The policy follows the same structure as the existing `security` (SECURITY.md) policy:

### `pkg/policies/secretscanning/secretscanning.go`
- Checks `Repository.SecurityAndAnalysis.SecretScanning.Status` via the GitHub REST API
- Passes if status is `"enabled"`, fails otherwise
- Handles nil `SecurityAndAnalysis` and nil `SecretScanning` gracefully
- Supports org-level and repo-level configuration via `secret_scanning.yaml`
- Supports `log`/`issue`/`fix` actions (fix logs a warning, not yet implemented)
- Notify text includes link to the repo's security settings page

### `pkg/policies/secretscanning/secretscanning_test.go`
- Tests for: enabled, disabled, nil SecurityAndAnalysis, nil SecretScanning

### `pkg/policies/policies.go`
- Registered `secretscanning.NewSecretScanning()` in `GetPolicies()`

## Configuration

Org-level (`.allstar/secret_scanning.yaml`):
```yaml
optConfig:
  optOutStrategy: true
action: issue
```

Repo-level (`.allstar/secret_scanning.yaml`):
```yaml
optConfig:
  optOut: true  # to opt out of this check
```

Fixes #363

body:
## Summary
Enhanced the i18n translation system to support default values and object return types, improving flexibility in translation handling across the application.

## Key Changes
- **i18n.t() method overloads**: Added TypeScript function overloads to support three calling patterns:
  - `t(key)` - returns string
  - `t(key, defaultValue)` - returns string with fallback default value
  - `t(key, { returnObjects: true })` - returns TranslationValue (object or string)

- **Default value support**: When a translation key is not found in primary or fallback languages, the provided default value is now returned instead of the key itself

- **Object return type handling**: Added `returnObjects` parameter to `getNestedValue()` to allow returning nested objects from translation files instead of only strings

- **React hook alignment**: Updated `useTranslation()` hook to properly type and forward the enhanced `t()` function with all overload signatures

- **Banner logic fix**: Changed prototype banner visibility check from strict equality (`=== 'true'`) to inequality (`!== 'false'`) for more intuitive default behavior

## Implementation Details
- The `getNestedValue()` method now conditionally returns resolved values as-is when `returnObjects` is true, otherwise filters to only string values
- Type safety is maintained through TypeScript function overloads in both the i18n class and React hook
- The implementation preserves backward compatibility while adding new optional features

body:
## Summary

Adds a per-invocation `--engine <name>` flag to `ft classify`, `ft classify-domains`, and `ft sync --classify`. Plumbs the choice into `resolveEngine({ override })` on `src/engine.ts`, which:

- Rejects unknown engine names with the known list.
- Fails fast if the named engine's binary isn't on PATH.
- Bypasses saved preferences and interactive prompting — overrides are strict.
- For `ft sync --classify --engine <name>`, runs the check before sync starts so a missing engine doesn't cost a full network sync.

Auto-resolution (no flag) is unchanged. `ft model` remains the way to set a persistent default; `--engine` is for cron/CI pinning and one-off overrides.

## Credit

Picks up the spirit of @ASRagab's #16, which was written on Apr 4 — three days before `src/engine.ts` landed in `3c28909`. That PR ended up stale against main (it added a parallel `resolveLlmEngine` in `bookmark-classify-llm.ts` that no longer exists on main), so this is a fresh take on top of the current engine abstraction. Thanks @ASRagab for the original design and tests — the override semantics here match your fail-fast intent.

## Diff

~95 lines vs #16's 236, because main already has cross-platform detection, preference persistence, and async invocation.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/engine.ts` | `resolveEngine()` now accepts `{ override?: string }` for strict per-invocation resolution |
| `src/cli.ts` | New `engineOption()` factory; `--engine` added to three commands; threaded through `classifyNew()` with pre-sync fail-fast |
| `tests/engine.test.ts` | Three new tests: unknown engine, missing binary, available binary |
| `README.md` | One-line doc in the Classification table |

author: crespocarlos
body:
## Summary

Converts two shell tools to Python, fixing two bugs that caused incorrect task resolution when multiple tasks exist on the same branch.

`resolve-task-dir.sh` was fighting shell's string-handling limitations throughout — it spawned 3 separate `python3 -c` subprocesses just to parse a single JSON file, and had two bugs in its multi-match tie-breaking logic: (1) the DONE-status check was case-sensitive (`"done"` never matched `"DONE"`, so completed tasks were never excluded from candidates), and (2) `created_at` values stored with escaped quotes (`"\"2026-...\""`  from the specwriter) sorted as "older" than clean dates, causing the wrong task to be returned. `log-progress.sh` had an optional `jq` dependency with messy shell string-escaping fallback just to produce a compact JSON object. Both are now pure Python using stdlib only.

All 11 call sites across skills, agents, rules, and CLAUDE.md are updated. The `.sh` files are deleted; `install.sh` adds cleanup to remove stale `.sh` symlinks on re-install.

### Identify risks

Drop-in replacement — identical CLI interface (`--remote`, `--branch`, `--all` for resolve-task-dir; positional `TASK_DIR TRANSITION` for log-progress). The two bug fixes change behavior only in the edge cases that were previously broken.

### How to test

- `python3 ~/.agent/tools/resolve-task-dir.py --help` — shows `--remote`, `--branch`, `--all`
- `python3 ~/.agent/tools/log-progress.py /tmp/test "APPROVED → IMPLEMENTING" && cat /tmp/test/PROGRESS.md` — shows correctly formatted line with no JSON suffix
- `CREW_WORKFLOW=build CREW_MEMBER=specwriter python3 ~/.agent/tools/log-progress.py /tmp/test2 "APPROVED → IMPLEMENTING" && cat /tmp/test2/PROGRESS.md` — line ends with ` {"step":"IMPLEMENTING","workflow":"build","crew":"specwriter"}`
- `grep -r "resolve-task-dir\.sh\|log-progress\.sh" ~/.cursor/` — no matches

---

## Summary

Add a real packaging and release lane for the UniFi provider so internal CI/CD consumers can install it without hand-building local mirrors.

## What Changed

- add `.github/workflows/package.yml` to build snapshot provider artifacts on PRs, `master`, and manual runs
- add `.github/workflows/release.yml` to publish tagged GitHub release assets
- add `scripts/build-release-artifacts.sh` to build cross-platform provider binaries and package them in Terraform mirror layout
- add `make release-artifacts VERSION=...`
- add `zip` to the Nix development shell so packaging works inside `nix develop`
- document internal usage in the README for both local `dev_overrides` and CI filesystem mirror installs

## Internal Consumption Model

The recommended internal artifact is:

- `terraform-provider-unifi_<version>_terraform-mirror.tar.gz`

That bundle contains Terraform's expected mirror layout under:

- `registry.terraform.io/badgerops/unifi/<version>/<os>_<arch>/...`

Internal pipelines can extract it and set `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` to a `filesystem_mirror` config, while local developers can use `dev_overrides` against a locally built binary.

## Verification

- `go test ./...`
- `nix develop --command bash -lc 'actionlint'`
- `nix develop --command bash -lc 'make release-artifacts VERSION=0.1.0-dev.2'`
- `terraform init` against the generated mirror tarball using a temporary `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`

## Follow-Up

The next improvement after this is adding automated version/tag discipline and, if desired, Terraform Registry publishing metadata. For internal use, the current mirror-bundle workflow is sufficient.

author: anasmadrhar
body:
## Summary

- **Wildcard `object_id`** — use glob patterns like `Wall_*` to target multiple 3D objects with a single entity binding
- **Static `opacity` field** — set material transparency on any entity binding once at load time, no HA entity state required

## Wildcard object_id matching

`object_id` now accepts `*` as a wildcard that matches any sequence of characters in an object name:

```yaml
object_id: 'Wall_*'          # all objects starting with Wall_
object_id: '*_ceiling'       # all ceiling objects
object_id: 'Room_*_floor'    # floor objects in any room
```

**How it works:** `_expandWildcardObjectIds()` runs once after the model loads (before entity setup), traverses the scene, and replaces each wildcard entry with every matching `THREE.Mesh` name. The rest of the entity pipeline sees a normal expanded list — no other code needed to change.

## Static opacity

Any entity binding now accepts an `opacity` field (0.0–1.0):

```yaml
entities:
  - entity: ''           # no HA entity needed for static effects
    type3d: color
    object_id: 'Wall_*'
    opacity: 0.4         # 40% opaque — 60% transparent
```

- Applied once at model load via `traverse()` so nested mesh hierarchies are handled

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

PostgreSQL throws error 42P18 ("could not determine data type of parameter $1") when executing queries like `SELECT value FROM super_settings WHERE key=$1`. The original placeholder conversion used `(_,i) => \`$${i+1}\`` which was doubly broken: it passed the character offset (not match index) as `i`, and it omitted the type cast that PostgreSQL needs to infer parameter types in simple WHERE clauses.

## Solution

Replaced the regex replacement in all three methods (`q.get`, `q.all`, `q.run`) with a local `paramIndex` counter and string concatenation: `() => '$' + (++paramIndex) + '::TEXT'`. The counter correctly numbers parameters sequentially from `$1`, and the `::TEXT` cast gives PostgreSQL the type hint it needs to plan the query without error.

### Changes
- **Modified** `database.js`

---
*Generated by [Railway](https://railway.com)*

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure PostgreSQL parameter placeholders are correctly numbered and typed when converting SQLite-style queries.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix incorrect PostgreSQL parameter indexing that could cause runtime errors when executing queries with placeholders.
- Cast converted PostgreSQL parameters to TEXT to avoid "could not determine data type of parameter" errors in simple WHERE clauses.

author: pandacooming
body:
## Summary

Prevents path traversal attacks (CVE-class) in profile archive extraction used by `hermes profile import` and `hermes claw migrate`. This closes a security gap where a maliciously crafted `.tar.gz` archive could write files outside the intended destination directory, potentially overwriting critical system files or injecting executables into `~/.hermes/`.

---

## Security Analysis

### Attack Vector

When a user runs `hermes profile import` (or `hermes claw migrate`) with a received archive file, an attacker who has prepared a specially crafted `.tar.gz` bundle could embed members with paths like:

| Member path | Extracted location |
|-------------|-------------------|
| `../../etc/cron.d/evil` | `/etc/cron.d/evil` |
| `/etc/passwd` | `/etc/passwd` |
| `~/.hermes/config.yaml` | Overwrites Hermes config |

This is a **path traversal (zip slip) vulnerability**.

### Defense Layers

**Layer 1 — Normalization-time (existing, preserved)**
`_normalize_profile_archive_parts()` rejects `..` components and absolute paths at parse time. This catches most attacks.

**Layer 2 — Extraction-time (new)**
`Path.is_relative_to(dest_resolved)` is checked **per-member at extraction time**, as a defense-in-depth measure that is robust against:
- Circular symlink attacks that can bypass `..` checks
- Symlink/hardlink exploitation (links can redirect a safe-looking path to a sensitive file)
- Edge cases in path normalization across platforms

Additionally, `member.issym()` and `member.islnk()` explicitly reject symlinks and hardlinks in archives, preventing attacks where a symlink `hermes.sh` → `/etc/passwd` is followed during extraction.

---

## Changes

### `hermes_cli/profiles.py`

| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| `import tarfile` moved to top-level | Removed 2 redundant local imports |
| `dest_resolved = destination.resolve()` moved out of loop | Resolves once, not per-member; minor perf improvement |
| `is_relative_to(dest_resolved)` check added | Secondary defense: fails if `member.name` resolves outside `destination` |
| Symlink/hardlink rejection | `member.issym() or member.islnk()` raises `ValueError` |
| `except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError)` | `ValueError` added to catch `is_relative_to()` failures; `RuntimeError` covers circular symlinks |

Error messages now include full resolved paths for debugging:
```
Archive member escapes destination: "../../etc/passwd" resolved to
"/etc/passwd", outside "/home/user/.hermes/profiles/migrate-import"
```

### `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py`

New `TestSafeExtractProfileArchive` class with 8 regression tests:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| `test_normal_extraction_succeeds` | Normal files extract cleanly |
| `test_nested_normal_path_ok` | Nested paths like `subdir/config.yaml` are allowed |
| `test_path_traversal_dot_dot_rejected` | `../../etc/cron.d/evil` → caught by Layer 1 |
| `test_path_traversal_absolute_rejected` | `/etc/passwd` → caught by Layer 1 |
| `test_symlink_rejected` | `SYMTYPE` tar entry → `"Unsupported archive member type"` |
| `test_hardlink_rejected` | `LNKTYPE` tar entry → `"Archive member is a link"` |
| `test_block_device_rejected` | `BLKTYPE` tar entry → `"Unsupported archive member type"` |
| `test_windows_absolute_path_rejected` | `C:\Windows\System32\evil` → caught by Layer 1 |

---

## Testing

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py::TestSafeExtractProfileArchive
  test_normal_extraction_succeeds ............................ PASSED
  test_nested_normal_path_ok ................................. PASSED
  test_path_traversal_dot_dot_rejected ....................... PASSED
  test_path_traversal_absolute_rejected ...................... PASSED
  test_symlink_rejected ...................................... PASSED
  test_hardlink_rejected ..................................... PASSED
  test_block_device_rejected .................................. PASSED
  test_windows_absolute_path_rejected ........................ PASSED

8 passed in ~1.35s
```

Full `hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` suite: **95 passed**, no regressions.

Bandit scan: **1 Low** (pre-existing `B110:try_except_pass` at `profiles.py:1003`, in the `rename_profile` function — unrelated to this change).

---

## Scope

- Affects: `hermes profile import`, `hermes claw migrate`
- Does not affect: `hermes backup` (uses `shutil` archive, not `tarfile`)
- Python version note: `Path.is_relative_to()` is available in Python 3.9+; the codebase already requires 3.9+

---

## Proof of Concept (for reviewers)

```python
import tarfile, tempfile, os
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.profiles import _safe_extract_profile_archive

# Craft malicious archive
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".tar.gz", delete=False) as f:
    tf = f.name
with tarfile.open(tf, "w:gz") as t:
    info = tarfile.TarInfo(name="../../tmp/evil.sh")
    info.size = 5
    t.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(b"evil"))

_safe_extract_profile_archive(Path(tf), Path("/tmp"))
# Before fix: /tmp/evil.sh created
# After fix: ValueError raised
os.unlink(tf)
```

---

## Checklist

- [x] 8 regression tests added covering traversal and link attack vectors
- [x] `is_relative_to()` extraction-time check added
- [x] Symlink/hardlink explicit rejection added
- [x] `tarfile` import consolidated to top-level
- [x] Error messages include resolved paths for debugging
- [x] Full profiles test suite passes (95/95)
- [x] Bandit scan: no high/critical findings
- [x] Single commit with conventional security prefix

author: elliotboney
body:
## Summary

- Vendor-aware filament subtype matching for the Qidi printer agent — filament subtypes
like "PLA+" are now matched to the correct OrcaSlicer profile using both vendor name and
filament name from the Qidi Box config file (e.g., "eSUN" + "PLA+" → eSUN PLA+ @base)
- Fix filament sync silently failing for all Moonraker-based printers — nozzle diameter
was defaulting to 0 (Moonraker doesn't report it), which caused get_printer_preset() to
fail matching and silently abort the sync

## Details

### Vendor-aware matching

The Qidi Box config file (officiall_filas_list.cfg) has two fields per filament entry:
filament (specific name like "PLA+") and type (base category like "PLA"). The agent now
parses both fields plus the [vendor_list] section, and uses a 3-tier matching strategy:

1. Try Qidi-specific QD_ setting ID
2. If vendor is known, search for a visible base preset whose name contains both vendor
and filament name
3. Fall back to filament_id_by_type using the base type

This follows OrcaSlicer's convention where PLA subtypes (Silk, Matte, PLA+) all use
filament_type: "PLA" and are distinguished by profile name only. Applies to all Qidi
printers that use the Qidi Box filament system.

### Nozzle diameter fix (all Moonraker printers)

Moonraker printers don't report nozzle size, so MachineObject's nozzle diameter defaults
to 0. This caused get_printer_preset() to never match (it requires both model ID and
nozzle diameter), making is_same_printer_for_connected_and_selected() return false and
silently abort sync. Fixed by setting the nozzle diameter from the selected printer
preset config in build_ams_payload(). This fix benefits all Moonraker-based printers, not
  just Qidi.

### Files changed

- [src/slic3r/Utils/QidiPrinterAgent.hpp](src/slic3r/Utils/QidiPrinterAgent.hpp) — added filament_types and vendors maps to
QidiFilamentDict, updated parse_filament_sections signature
- [src/slic3r/Utils/QidiPrinterAgent.cpp](src/slic3r/Utils/QidiPrinterAgent.cpp) — vendor+name matching helper, type field
parsing, vendor resolution in fetch_slot_info
- [src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp](src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp) — set nozzle diameter on DevNozzleSystem
from preset config in build_ams_payload

### Test plan

- Tested with Qidi Q2 + Qidi Box running 4 filament slots: 3x Generic PLA + 1x eSUN PLA+
- Slots correctly show "Generic PLA" for plain PLA and "eSUN PLA+" for vendor-matched
slot
- Sync toast message appears: "Successfully synchronized color and type of filament from
printer"
- Verify no regression on other Moonraker-based printers (Snapmaker, other Qidi models)
- Verify no regression on Bambu Lab printers

body:
(AI Generated).

## Summary
- serialize desktop Automerge worker mutations so whole-document save and hydrate work cannot overlap under load
- treat failed preference persistence as non-fatal diagnostics instead of escalating to the fatal recovery screen
- downgrade benign `ResizeObserver` window errors to warnings so browser noise does not crash Freed Desktop
- add regression tests for both the non-fatal preferences path and the benign `ResizeObserver` capture path

## Root cause
Two separate recovery paths were too aggressive.

First, the desktop Automerge worker could process async requests while earlier expensive save and hydrate work was still in flight, which made preference updates vulnerable to timing out under background load.

Second, the global runtime error capture treated the known browser `ResizeObserver` loop warning as a fatal application error, so a benign window error could trip the crash screen.

## Impact
These changes make Freed Desktop much harder to knock into the fatal recovery screen during long-running sessions, especially while background scrapers or other heavy document work are active.

body: Real-time typing and recording indicators for WhatsApp contacts connected via the baileys-api provider. When a contact starts typing or recording audio in WhatsApp, agents see the indicator both in the conversation view ("X is typing" / "X is recording audio") and in the chat list ("typing..." / "recording..." in green text replacing the message preview), similar to the native WhatsApp experience. ## How to test 1. Go to inbox settings for a baileys WhatsApp inbox, enable "Show contact typing indicators" 2. Reconnect the channel (manage connection) 3. Open a conversation with a WhatsApp contact 4. Have the contact type or record audio in WhatsApp 5. Observe the typing/recording indicator in both the conversation view and the chat list ## What changed - **Presence update handler** (`presence_update.rb`): Processes `presence.update` webhook events from baileys-api, maps presence states to typing events, consolidates contact LID from the `jidAlt` payload - **Recording event**: Added `conversation.recording` to ActionCable, webhook, and channel listeners for full parity with `typing_on`/`typing_off` - **Chat list indicator**: Green "typing..." / "recording..." text replaces message preview in `ConversationCard` - **Presence subscribe**: New `presence_subscribe` provider config option (default off) gates all subscription calls. author: rickisba
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a dedicated RPS-mode sender to model KVCache injection timing and produce per-request timing/size statistics for injection-hit prediction and capacity analysis.
- Allow the sender to resolve knowledge lengths accurately by optionally peeking the scheduler `/debug/knowledge/peek` endpoint to avoid fallback heuristics.
- Expose a CLI tool that can be used to generate JSONL/CSV outputs for downstream modeling and performance analysis under controlled RPS loads.

### Description
- Add `client/kv_timing_sender.py`, an async RPS-driven task sender that posts workload requests, collects cacheroute meta, and computes a detailed timing/size record per request.
- Implement knowledge-length resolution that prefers explicit `knowledge_length_tokens`, then scheduler peek results, and finally falls back to `total_length_tokens`, with enforced 256-token alignment for hit length.
- Use the existing `queue_predictor` to estimate remaining text compute time and derive `lmcache_redis_pull_ms`, and produce outputs including `request_id`, `predict_length_tokens`, `actual_hit_length_tokens`, `remaining_compute_tokens`, `kvcache_size_gb`, `queue_wait_ms`, `compute_ms`, `text_compute_estimate_ms`, `lmcache_redis_pull_ms`, and `total_ms`.
- Update `client/README.md` to document the new `kv_timing_sender.py` usage, CLI flags, output formats, and the algorithmic behavior for knowledge-length sourcing and alignment.

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or executed for this change.

author: luciemise
body:
This PR introduces the initial data exploration and preparation phase for a credit risk scoring system. The objective of this work is to understand borrower characteristics, identify key drivers of default risk, and prepare the dataset for downstream modeling.

The dataset consists of historical lending data, with the goal of predicting borrower default and supporting data-driven lending decisions.

#### Problem Context
In lending, inaccurate credit decisions can lead to increased default rates and financial losses. This project aims to build a predictive system that helps:

* Identify high-risk borrowers
* Improve loan approval decisions
* Balance portfolio growth with credit risk

#### Scope of this PR

This PR covers:
* Data loading and initial inspection
* Target variable definition
* Data cleaning and type corrections
* Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
* Initial feature assessment and correlation analysis

#### Key Changes
1. Target Variable Definition
Converted `loan_status`  into a binary target:
*  0 → Fully Paid (non-default)
* 1 → Charged Off (default)
This aligns the dataset with a supervised learning classification setup.


2. Data Cleaning
Addressed inconsistencies in data types:
Converted term from string (e.g., "36 months") to numeric
This step ensure compatibility with machine learning models and improve data quality.

3. Dataset Characteristics
* Size: 396030 records
* Features: ~27 variables
*  Target distribution:
      * ~80% non-default
      * ~20% default
This reflects a realistic and moderately imbalanced credit dataset.

#### Key Insights
* Interest rate is strongly associated with default risk
Higher interest rates correspond to higher default probability, reflecting risk-based pricing in lending.
* Debt-to-income ratio is a critical risk indicator
Borrowers with higher DTI show increased likelihood of default due to higher financial burden.
* Loan grade is a strong predictor of creditworthiness
Lower grades exhibit significantly higher default rates, validating internal risk scoring mechanisms.
* Income alone is not a sufficient predictor
Income must be evaluated in conjunction with debt-related features to assess repayment capacity.
* Loan purpose influences risk patterns
Certain loan categories (e.g., small business) exhibit higher default rates.

#### Correlation Analysis

Correlation analysis was performed on numeric variables to identify relationships with the target.

#### Key findings:

* Positive correlation: int_rate, dti → higher risk
* Weak or mixed correlation: annual_inc → requires feature interaction

Categorical variables were excluded from correlation and will be encoded in subsequent steps.

#### Limitations
* Correlation does not imply causation
* Some important features are categorical and not captured in correlation analysis
* Dataset contains class imbalance that will need to be addressed during modeling

## Summary

- **Restructured execute SKILL.md** from ~2,800 words to ~830-word lean decision tree using progressive disclosure. Procedural details moved to `references/team-execution.md` and `references/sequential-execution.md` — loaded on-demand, reducing context pressure that causes orchestrator shortcutting
- **Added mandatory Delegation Rules section** front-and-center in SKILL.md with explicit tool selection table (TeamCreate for stories, Agent for workflow steps) and the callout: "Using Agent to execute stories is a protocol violation"
- **Added PreToolUse compliance hook** (`hooks/check-agent-misuse.sh`) that deterministically blocks Agent tool calls containing story-level execution patterns before they execute. Tested against 6 scenarios — correctly blocks story/epic-level Agent misuse while allowing legitimate within-story Agent calls

## Motivation

The orchestrator frequently violates delegation protocols during execute phase — doing implementation work directly or using Agent instead of TeamCreate for story-level parallelization. This is a context pressure problem (too many competing instructions in one file) compounded by lack of enforcement.

This PR addresses both root causes:
1. **Soft:** Progressive disclosure reduces competing context at decision time
2. **Medium:** Explicit delegation rules make the correct tool choice unmissable
3. **Hard:** PreToolUse hook blocks the wrong tool call before it executes

## Test plan

- [x] Hook tested with 6 scenarios (3 block, 3 allow)

body:
### Motivation
- Enforce consistent canonical keys and active-row uniqueness for `account` and `fund` to prevent ambiguous postings and reporting drift. 
- Introduce deterministic import-time matching and governance for aliases to remove fragile ad-hoc mappings and enable safe cutover to strict uniqueness. 
- Provide operational tooling for triage/backfill of ambiguous aliases so cutover can be staged without breaking imports.

### Description
- Added forward migration SQL `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_forward.sql` that creates `alias_review_queue`, hygiene `CHECK` constraints, active-row normalized unique indexes, alias FK constraints, and an initial population step that enqueues active alias collisions.
- Added rollback SQL `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_rollback.sql` that drops the introduced indexes/constraints and the `alias_review_queue` table.
- Added validation SQL `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_validation.sql` with deterministic checks for blank keys, duplicate normalized active keys, alias collisions, and governance queue state.
- Added documentation: `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_proposal.md` (naming/key standards, dedupe rules, deterministic matching pseudocode, backfill plan) and `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_risk_register.md` (rollout/operational risks and mitigations).

author: mittalrishabh
body:
## Summary

- Implement `ChunkEvictionManager` for removing cold chunks from NVMe while keeping them durable on S3
- `evict_chunk(chunk_id)` verifies S3 durability, blocks writes during eviction, flushes dirty data, releases NVMe space, and updates chunk state
- Thread-safe per-chunk locking supports concurrent evictions; rollback on failure restores NORMAL state
- Bitmap stays valid after eviction — only the data location changes
- After eviction, reads fall through to S3 via TieredReadHandler (Task 2.1 / PR #5)

## New Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `chunk_eviction_manager.h` | `ChunkEvictionManager`, `NvmeChunkManager` callback interface, `EvictionResult` enum, metrics |
| `chunk_eviction_manager.cpp` | Implementation: evict flow, state machine, dirty flush, rollback |
| `test_chunk_eviction.cpp` | 13 unit tests |

## Test Plan

- [x] Successful eviction: NVMe released, chunk marked evicted
- [x] Rejection: chunk not on S3
- [x] Rejection: chunk already evicted
- [x] Dirty data flushed to S3 before eviction
- [x] Reads after eviction go to S3 (via TieredReadHandler integration)
- [x] Bitmap/superblock entry unchanged after eviction
- [x] NVMe release failure rolls back to NORMAL
- [x] `mark_hydrated()` restores chunk after re-hydration
- [x] Concurrent evictions of different chunks
- [x] Concurrent evictions of same chunk (only one succeeds)
- [x] Write blocked during eviction state
- [x] Unknown chunk queries return false

author: thelollipopman
body:
## Summary

- Implemented stochastic patient death using logistic regression (age, √tumour burden, organ metastasis) with Bernoulli sampling per tick
- Added patient outcome state (`dead` / `cured`) and terminated simulation upon either condition
- Introduced transformed tumour burden (√) for regression while preserving raw count for UI
- Computed organ metastasis as sum of squared organ tumour fractions (lungs combined)
- Lowered metastasis threshold and replaced fixed probability with continuous probability increasing with organ fraction
- Reduced metastasis cooldown from 150 → 50 ticks
- Included metastatic cells in organ tumour counts
- Updated UI with terminal state overlay and disabled interactions after outcome

author: copilot
body:
Adds real LLM-powered game creation to the chatbot: `create game: <idea>` now calls OpenAI `gpt-4o`, generates a self-contained `launchGame(container)` JS function, and reveals the playable game after a 5-minute countdown. Includes per-user API key management and a 10-games/day rate limit.

## Settings Panel
- ⚙️ button added to nav; opens a modal for entering/saving the OpenAI API key to `localStorage`
- If no key is set, `create game:` returns: *"🔑 Please set your OpenAI API key in ⚙️ Settings first!"*

## Daily Limit Tracking
- `getDailyCount()` / `incrementDailyCount()` persist `{ gameCreationDate, gameCreationCount }` in `localStorage`, auto-resetting on date change
- At 10 games: *"🚫 You've reached your 10 game limit for today! Come back tomorrow."*

## LLM Game Generation Flow
- `callOpenAI(gameIdea)` fires immediately on submission; response is held until the 5-minute countdown completes
- Countdown ticks live in chat: *"⏳ Generating "…"... 04:47 remaining"*
- On countdown end: game is revealed in Game Hub; if API hasn't resolved yet, `waitForApiAndReveal()` polls every 5s up to `MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS = 60`
- LLM prompt instructs the model to return **only** a raw `launchGame(container)` function — no markdown, no explanation

## Secure Game Execution
- LLM-returned code runs inside a sandboxed `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` — fully isolated from the parent page, no DOM/cookie/localStorage access
- Replaces the previous `new Function()` approach

## Game Hub UX
- Pending game cards show a pulsing "⏳ Generating…" badge
- Clicking a generating card redirects to chatbot with a friendly wait message
- Failed generation surfaces the API error (with user-friendly messages for 401/429)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Integrate a Real LLM into Chore Quest Hub for AI Game Generation

The repository `carterobviously-creator/work` is a GitHub Pages static site (Chore Quest Hub) with a chatbot, game hub, chore tracker, break timer, and AI buddy.

### Feature: Real LLM-Powered Game Creation

Integrate a real LLM (using the **OpenAI API** via a client-side fetch call) into the chatbot so that when a user types `create game: [description]`, it:

1. **Calls the OpenAI API** (model: `gpt-4o` or `gpt-3.5-turbo`) with a prompt asking it to generate a fully playable HTML5 canvas JavaScript game based on the user's description.
2. **Shows a "generating" state** in the chatbot for **5 minutes** (300 seconds) with a countdown — e.g. "⏳ Generating your game... 4:47 remaining" — to simulate the build time. During this time the game is actually being generated by the LLM in the background.
3. **Limits game creation to 10 games per day** — tracked in `localStorage` with a date stamp. If the user has already created 10 games today, show a friendly message: "🚫 You've reached your 10 game limit for today! Come back tomorrow."
4. **When the 5-minute countdown finishes**, the new game appears in the Game Hub as a fully playable game. The LLM should return self-contained JavaScript game code that runs on an HTML5 canvas element.
5. **The LLM prompt** should instruct the model to return ONLY a JavaScript function called `launchGame(container)` that creates a canvas game inside the provided DOM container element. No markdown, no explanation — just the raw JS function.

### Implementation Details

Since this is a **static GitHub Pages site** (no backend), the OpenAI API key will be entered by the user in a settings panel:

- Add a ⚙️ **Settings button** (top right of the nav bar)
- Settings panel has an input for the OpenAI API key, saved to `localStorage`
- If no API key is set, the `create game:` command shows: "🔑 Please set your OpenAI API key in ⚙️ Settings first!"

### Game Generation Flow

1. User types: `create game: a platformer where you jump over spikes`
2. Bot replies: `🎮 Game creation started! ⏳ Generating "a platformer where you jump over spikes"... Check back in 5 minutes!`
3. A countdown timer appears in the chat: `⏳ 4:59 remaining...` updating every second
4. In the background, the actual OpenAI API call is made immediately (it takes seconds, not 5 minutes — but the result is held and revealed after the 5-minute countdown)
5. After 5 minutes, bot says: `🎉 Your game "a platformer where you jump over spikes" is ready! Head to the 🎮 Game Hub to play it!`
6. The game appears in the Game Hub and is fully playable

### Daily Limit Tracking

In `localStorage`, store:
```json
{
  "gameCreationDate": "2026-04-13",
  "gameCreationCount": 3
}
```
Reset count to 0 when the date changes.

### LLM Prompt Template

```
You are a game developer. Generate a complete, self-contained JavaScript function called `launchGame(container)` that creates a fun, playable HTML5 canvas game inside the provided DOM element `container`. 

Game idea: ${userGameIdea}

Requirements:
- Create a canvas element, append it to container
- The game must be fully playable with keyboard or mouse controls
- Include score display, win/lose conditions
- Use bright colors on a dark background
- Keep it under 200 lines of JavaScript
- Return ONLY the raw JavaScript function, no markdown, no explanation, no code fences
```

### Files to modify:
- `app.js` — Add LLM integration, countdown timer logic, daily limit tracking, settings panel logic
- `index.html` — Add settings button/panel to the nav area
- `styles.css` — Add styles for settings panel, countdown timer in chat, game generation status

Make sure everything still works as a static GitHub Pages site with no build step required.

author: yilu331
body:
## Summary
- Upgrade the OpenClaw integration to match Claude Code integration maturity: multi-user support, agent playbook aggregation, per-message search, and skill-driven publishing
- Each OpenClaw agent instance (identified by `agentId`) becomes a unique Reflexio user — playbooks and profiles are isolated per-instance, while agent playbooks are shared across all instances
- Single expert mode (no normal/expert split) — one unified set of skill, hook, rule, and commands covers search, publish, and aggregation
- Follows the 4-component integration pattern from `agent-integration-design.md`: Skill (procedural guidance), Hook (deterministic enforcement), Rule (behavioral constraints), Command (user-triggered actions)

## Changes

### Hook (`handler.ts`)
- Renamed from `handler.js` to `handler.ts` — OpenClaw's hook loader compiles TypeScript at gateway startup; `.ts` is the canonical handler format
- Add `resolveUserId(event)` with 4-step fallback chain: env var → sessionKey agentId → OpenClaw config → "openclaw" default
- Add `handleSearchBeforeResponse` for per-message `message:received` search injection (5s timeout, skips short/trivial prompts)
- Add `triggerAggregationIfNeeded()` — fire-and-forget aggregation after successful publish with flag file concurrency guard
- Add `ensureServerRunning()` — auto-starts local Reflexio server at bootstrap and on search connection errors (same pattern as Claude Code's session_start_hook.sh)
- Added `package-lock.json` for reproducible npm installs of `better-sqlite3`

### Skill (`SKILL.md`)
- Complete rewrite as unified expert-mode skill: search before tasks + publish on corrections/completions
- Two publish scenarios: (1) user correction with rich context, (2) key step completion with learnings
- Agent playbook commands, multi-user concept, server management

### Rule (`rules/reflexio.md`) — new
- Always-active behavioral constraints loaded at every session start
- Tells agent to follow injected `REFLEXIO_CONTEXT` blocks from the search hook
- Manual search fallback when hook doesn't fire
- Enforces transparency (never mention Reflexio), non-blocking (proceed if unavailable), silent infrastructure (never ask user to manage server)

### Commands — new
- `/reflexio-extract` — manual comprehensive conversation extraction
- `/reflexio-aggregate` — manual playbook aggregation trigger with cron guidance

### CLI fixes
- Fix `reflexio search` to surface agent playbooks (was passing `user_playbooks` as `agent_playbooks`)
- Add `user_playbooks` parameter to `format_context()` output formatter

### Setup wizard (`setup_cmd.py`)
- One-command install (`reflexio setup openclaw`) and uninstall (`reflexio setup openclaw --uninstall`) for all 4 components
- Hook installed by copying (not symlinking) — works around OpenClaw symlink discovery bug (GitHub #11861)
- Dynamic command discovery in both install and uninstall

### Documentation
- **README.md**: Fully rewritten with multi-user architecture, agent playbooks, cron guidance, all 4 integration components
- **TESTING.md** (new): Step-by-step manual testing guide covering 8 phases — install, auto-start, cold-start search, capture/publish, warm-start retrieval, manual commands, multi-user isolation, graceful degradation, uninstall

### Eval suite — new
- 8 evaluation scenarios: correction capture, retrieval, multi-user isolation, aggregation dedup, search relevance, tool failure extraction, cron aggregation, graceful degradation
- Data-driven runner with JSON dataset and dispatch table

### E2E tests — new
- 10 tests across 4 classes: multi-user, aggregation, unified search, graceful degradation

## Known Limitations
- **Hook events**: `message:received` and `message:sent` only fire in channel sessions (Telegram, WhatsApp, etc.) — not in CLI (`openclaw agent -m`) or TUI mode. This is an OpenClaw architectural limitation where these events are emitted from `dispatchReplyFromConfig()` (channel dispatch path only). The skill and rule provide fallback coverage for non-channel modes.
- **Rule loading**: Custom `.md` files in `~/.openclaw/workspace/` are not loaded as workspace context — OpenClaw only loads specific named files (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, etc.). The rule content may need to be appended to `AGENTS.md` instead.

## Test Plan
- [x] All 10 E2E tests passing: `uv run pytest tests/e2e_tests/test_openclaw_integration.py -o 'addopts='`
- [x] Ruff linting clean on all modified Python files
- [x] Review-fix loop completed (6 findings found and fixed, all verified)
- [x] Hook loads in OpenClaw gateway (6/6 ready after handler.ts rename + copy install)
- [x] `agent:bootstrap` fires correctly in all modes (CLI, TUI, channel)
- [x] Server auto-start triggers on bootstrap when local server is down
- [x] Skills discovered: `reflexio`, `reflexio-extract`, `reflexio-aggregate` all ✓ ready
- [ ] Manual channel-based testing (Telegram) for `message:received`/`message:sent` events
- [ ] Manual testing via [TESTING.md](reflexio/integrations/openclaw/TESTING.md)

author: tschonleber
body:
## Summary

Closes the biggest correctness gap in the project: **`Brain.remember()` was bypassing the W(m) worthiness gate entirely.** The Python API, LangChain/CrewAI integrations, and the new Hermes plugin were all doing raw `INSERT`s while only the MCP path enforced surprise scoring, semantic dedup, arousal coupling, and valence-gated encoding. This PR makes the advertised cognitive-architecture filtering actually run on the default write path.

Also fixes four smaller-but-real correctness bugs uncovered by the audit: reconsolidation-window writes from other agents, trigger substring false-positives, `_safe_fts` destroying phrase/prefix/boolean queries, and silent `OperationalError` swallows hiding schema corruption.

## Why

From the codebase audit:

1. `brain.py:157` did a raw `INSERT` — the entire `_gates.run_write_gate()` pipeline only ran via MCP.
2. `_is_labile()` was a read-side recall booster only; a different agent could overwrite a memory while the 20-minute reconsolidation window was open for someone else.
3. `check_triggers()` used `if k in query_lower` — "deploy" fired on "redeploy", "re" fired on "research".
4. `_safe_fts()` stripped every non-word character and OR-joined — destroyed `"release notes"` phrase searches, killed `api*` prefix matches, and on input like `"- - -"` produced `OR OR OR` → FTS5 syntax error.
5. `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass` hid FTS5 failures behind LIKE fallbacks with zero log signal.

## What changed

### 1. W(m) gate wired into the Python API (`brain.py` + `_gates.py`)

- New `_gates.evaluate_write(...)` as the canonical gate entry point, used by both `Brain.remember()` and (eventually) the MCP write path. Returns a `GateDecision` with `accepted` / `reason` / scores.
- New `_gates.GateDecision` dataclass + module-level helpers for surprise, arousal, valence, source trust.
- `Brain.remember()` signature extended: `remember(content, category="general", tags=None, confidence=1.0, *, bypass_gate=False, strict=False, supersedes_id=None, source=None)`.
  - Default behavior: gate runs; rejection emits `_log.warning` and returns `None`.
  - `bypass_gate=True` skips the gate (migration tools / tests).
  - `strict=True` raises `GateRejected` instead of returning `None`.
- New `GateRejected` exception exported from `agentmemory.brain`.
- New private helpers: `_embed_for_gate()`, `_get_vec_db()`, `_log_gate_rejection()`.

### 2. Reconsolidation lability window enforced on writes

- `is_labile()` moved from `mcp_tools_consolidation.py` into `_gates.py`; old site keeps a re-export for back-compat.
- New `_gates.check_lability_block(memory_id, writing_agent_id)` fires during gate evaluation: if `labile_until > now()` and `labile_agent_id != writing_agent`, the write is rejected.

### 3. Trigger word-boundary fix (`brain.py:518-520`)

```python
# before
if k in query_lower
# after
if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(k)}\b", query_lower)
```

### 4. `_safe_fts()` rewrite (`brain.py:64`)

Real FTS5 sanitizer (pure Python, no new deps) that:
- Preserves quoted phrases: `"release notes"` stays a phrase
- Preserves prefix matching: `api*` stays a prefix
- Strips unbalanced quotes and parens
- Returns empty string on degenerate input (only punctuation) — caller already handles empty correctly

### 5. Error-swallow logging

Every `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass` in `search()`, `orient()`, `check_triggers()` now emits a `_log.warning(...)` with the exception and site before falling through.

## Test plan

New `tests/test_phase0_correctness.py` — **15 tests, all passing**:

- [x] **Gate parity** — `Brain.remember(...)` and MCP `memory_remember` reject the same inputs and produce the same rejection reasons (with forced surprise scores on both sides to avoid the non-deterministic LIKE probe in mcp_server)
- [x] `bypass_gate=True` inserts unconditionally
- [x] `strict=True` raises `GateRejected` on rejection
- [x] Reconsolidation window: agent A opens lability, agent B's write to the same memory is rejected; agent A's own write succeeds
- [x] Trigger boundary: "redeploy" does NOT fire a "deploy" trigger; "the deploy failed" does
- [x] `_safe_fts('"release notes"')` returns a valid FTS5 phrase query
- [x] `_safe_fts("api*")` returns a valid prefix query
- [x] `_safe_fts("- - -")` returns `""`
- [x] OperationalError fallthroughs log warnings

Suite-wide:
- Full suite: **1337 passed, 1 skipped** in 245.97s
- `tests/test_brain.py::test_confidence` adjusted to pass `bypass_gate=True`: `confidence=0.4` alone now falls below the pre-worthiness floor (0.289 < 0.3), which is **pre-existing MCP behavior** the Python API previously bypassed. This is a correctness fix surfacing, not a regression.

## Surprises worth flagging

- `mcp_server.tool_memory_add` computes surprise via `list(set(...))[:5]` as a LIKE probe — hash-ordered and non-deterministic. Parity tests monkeypatch `_word_overlap_surprise` and `_surprise_score_mcp` to forced values. Still a true parity check (same forced surprise → same floor → same math).
- Pre-worthiness floor × neutral arousal × source_trust means `confidence ≤ 0.4` is auto-rejected. Real UX wart that predates this PR — worth revisiting next time the gate math is tuned.

## Follow-ups (explicitly out of scope)

- **`mcp_server.tool_memory_add` (lines 487-640) still duplicates the gate logic inline** instead of calling `_gates.evaluate_write()`. Task scope said "reference only" for that file. Follow-up PR should route MCP through the same helper so parity is enforced **structurally**, not by mirrored code.
- `doctor()` still uses generic `except Exception: pass` around count queries — different pattern from the in-scope `OperationalError` swallows, left alone.
- Pre-worthiness floor UX (low-confidence + neutral arousal → auto-reject) needs a tuning pass.
- `collapse_mechanics.py` / `agent_beliefs` wiring is still Phase 4.

## Commit

- Branch: `claude/phase0-correctness`
- Commit: `64d6362`

## What this is

The user flow audit you asked for, executed.

PRs #6, #7, #10, #11 (the original #8 and #9 reopened) are all merged. This branch is built on top of that final main and removes the structural cruft that accumulated.

**No copy changes. No product behavior changes.** Same Sam, same prompt, same quiz, same paywall. Just a simpler structure underneath.

## Before vs after

**Before:**
- `/chat` was a 4-way state machine: `board | chat | checkin | voice`
- Auth'd users landed on the Dashboard "hub" view first, had to click "Talk to Sam" to actually use the product
- Returning users had no way to log back in (no `/signin` page existed)
- `/chat/page.tsx` was ~400 lines with nested conditionals, an anonymous localStorage fallback, and View-mode switching

**After:**
- `/chat` is the workspace. One view: split-pane chat + tasks on desktop, single-column chat on mobile
- Voice is an overlay toggled by a mic button in the chat header
- Returning users hit `/signin` (linked from the marketing landing) to log in
- `/chat/page.tsx` is ~210 lines of pure handler logic. Two modes only: chat (default) and voice (overlay)

## Files

| Change | File |
|---|---|
| **NEW** | `src/app/signin/page.tsx` — sign-in page for returning users |
| Updated | `src/components/MarketingLanding.tsx` — added "Already have an account? Sign in" link |
| Updated | `src/middleware.ts` — added `/signin` to redirect-away-if-authed list, deduplicated subscription queries |
| Rewrote | `src/app/chat/page.tsx` — removed board mode, Dashboard, View state machine, anonymous fallback. Two modes only. |
| Updated | `src/components/TextConversation.tsx` — added optional `onOpenVoice` and `onSignOut` props for the workspace header |
| Deleted | `src/lib/useTaskStore.ts` — no remaining references after the anonymous fallback was removed |
| Kept on disk | `src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — only used by `/demo` (legacy tech demo) |

## Net diff: +173 / -409 lines

## Test results

- TypeScript: clean
- Vitest: **92/93 pass** (1 pre-existing voice ID test unrelated)
- Production build: passes
- `/simplify` + `/code-review` gate: clean, no real findings

## What you'll see when you test

### Cold visitor flow (new user via Meta ad)
`/` (marketing) → quiz → checkout → `/success` (OTP) → `/chat` (workspace, immediate)

### Returning user flow (the gap that was missing)
`/` → click "Sign in" → `/signin` (OTP only) → `/chat` (workspace, immediate)

### Already-signed-in user
Any URL → middleware sends them to `/chat`

### Voice
Inside the workspace, click the mic icon in the chat header → full-screen voice overlay → click Back → return to workspace with state preserved

### Sign out
Inside the workspace, click "Sign out" in the header → back to marketing landing

## Manual verification checklist

- [ ] Visit `/` as an unauthenticated user — see marketing landing with "Sign in" link in footer
- [ ] Click "Sign in" → land on `/signin` → enter email → get OTP code → enter it → arrive at `/chat`
- [ ] Visit `/chat` as an unauthenticated user — middleware redirects to `/`
- [ ] Visit `/` as an authenticated paid user — middleware redirects to `/chat`
- [ ] Visit `/signin` as an authenticated paid user — middleware redirects to `/chat`
- [ ] On `/chat`, you land directly on the workspace (no Dashboard step)
- [ ] On desktop, see chat + focus panel side-by-side
- [ ] On mobile, see chat with collapsible task bar at bottom
- [ ] Click the mic button in the header → enter voice mode → click Back → return to chat with state intact
- [ ] Click "Sign out" → back to `/` marketing landing
- [ ] Type a brain dump → tasks appear in the focus panel → check one off → still done after refresh

author: stevenbtw
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #267 #268 #155 

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---
## Summary by cubic
Adds quantized vector indexes for up to 4x lower memory, completes EXPLAIN/ANALYZE across all query languages, and hardens parsers with nesting limits and Unicode identifier/escape support. Fixes incremental backups after full backups, corrects edge variable outputs, stabilizes ranking tie‑breakers to remove flaky tests, fixes weighted hybrid search ranking (#267, #268, #155), exposes the `ring-index` feature for compact RDF, and bumps the workspace and bindings to v0.5.38 with dependency updates.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Incremental backups after a full backup now work by rotating the WAL at the end of `backup_full` and `backup_incremental` (#267). Added a regression test.
  - Edge variables in expand chains return full edge maps (`_id`, `_type`, `_source`, `_target`, props) instead of raw IDs (#268). Added a regression test.
  - Weighted `hybrid_search` no longer inverts vector ranking; distances are negated before fusion so closer vectors score higher (related to #155). Added tests for MMR/vector distance parity and hybrid ordering.
  - Query correctness and safety: max nesting depth across Cypher, GQL, GraphQL, Gremlin, SPARQL, and SQL/PGQ; Unicode identifiers plus `\u`/`\U` escapes; GQL lexer handles `!=`; SPARQL `SERVICE` clearly errors as unsupported; Turtle imports avoid blank‑node ID collisions.
  - Stable tie‑breaking for equal scores/distances to eliminate flaky test ordering.

- **New Features**
  - Quantized vector indexes via `create_vector_index(..., quantization="scalar"|"binary"|"product")` with unified `VectorIndexKind`; bindings updated in Python, Node, WASM, and C.
  - `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` prefixes supported in GraphQL, Gremlin, and SQL/PGQ translators (now all six languages).
  - Python: `AsyncQueryResult` adds `nodes()`/`edges()`; `PyQueryResult.to_ntriples()` exports SPARQL CONSTRUCT results; docs add guides for Text Search (BM25), Hybrid Search (RRF and weighted), and MMR; clarified that `vector_search`/`mmr_search` return distances (lower = better) while `text_search`/`hybrid_search` return scores (higher = better); documented vector index auto-sync and when to use `rebuild*Index()`.
  - `grafeo` crate ergonomics: new `ring-index` feature (enables compact RDF Ring Index, depends on `triple-store`), and top-level re-exports for common modules/types (`admin`, optional `cdc`, `database`, `session`, `memory_usage`, `MemoryUsage`, `ProjectionSpec`). Release/deps: bumped workspace and all bindings/CLI to 0.5.38; updated `softprops/action-gh-release` to v3 and minor Rust deps (`hashbrown`, `indexmap`, `clap_complete`).

<sup>Written for commit 038f0c63b33b38e2adb795ed015f12183c9f03a7. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>

author: xmarre
body:
## Summary
- narrow resident safetensors diffusion-model loads to detected UNet tensors instead of loading the whole file and filtering afterward
- add loader-keyed live-object reuse in the residency registry and thread it through the resident diffusion and checkpoint loaders
- add staged checkpoint model, CLIP, and VAE resident nodes while keeping the full checkpoint loader and improving kind-aware sticky/offload policy behavior

## Root Cause
The resident loader was optimizing final placement but not the width of the hot path. Safetensors diffusion-model loads still materialized full state dicts before filtering, checkpoint loading remained monolithic, and the registry tracked residency metadata without any loader-facing fast cache hit path.

## Validation
- `python3 -m py_compile kj_loader.py patches.py residency.py nodes.py`
- `mcp__ouroboros__ouroboros_qa` against the patch-specific acceptance bar (PASS, score 0.86)
- repository tests were not run per repo instruction


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Three resident checkpoint loaders: model, CLIP, and VAE; staged component loading and reuse to avoid redundant full-checkpoint loads.
  * Live-object reuse across resident loads for faster repeated ingests.
  * Selective UNet loading for .safetensors to speed model-only ingests and reduce memory use.

* **Documentation**

body:
💡 **What:** Refactored the `SetFieldValuesForMultipleRowsAsync` and `ScaleFieldValuesForMultipleRowsAsync` methods in `EtabsTableEditingService.cs` to use a pre-built dictionary lookup instead of a nested `FirstOrDefault` iteration over `rows`.
🎯 **Why:** To drastically improve the performance of bulk row edits. Searching through `rows` using `FirstOrDefault` inside a `foreach` loop resulted in an inefficient `O(N*M)` time complexity, which scales poorly on large tables. Pre-building the dictionary brings the time complexity down to `O(N+M)`.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** We constructed a benchmark simulating a 10,000 row table receiving 1,000 updates.
- **Baseline (O(N*M))**: ~238 ms
- **Optimized (O(N+M))**: ~9 ms
- **Improvement**: Execution time reduced by over **96%**.

## Summary

- **auto-release.yml**: Instead of pushing the version bump commit directly to `main`, creates a temporary branch (`auto-release/vX.Y.Z`), opens a PR, and enables auto-merge (squash). Once the 3 required status checks (Lint, Test, CodeQL) pass, the PR auto-merges and `release.yml` picks up the `chore: release vX.Y.Z` commit as before.
- **prepare-release.yml**: Same fix — creates a PR with auto-merge instead of direct push.
- Added `pull-requests: write` permission to both jobs (needed for `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge --auto`).

## Root cause

The `auto-release` job failed at the "Commit and push" step with:

```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
remote: - Changes must be made through a pull request.
remote: - 3 of 3 required status checks are expected.
```

The "Protect main" ruleset (id: 14939624) enforces:
1. All changes via pull request (no direct pushes)
2. Required status checks: Lint, Test (ubuntu-latest, 22.x), CodeQL

Both `auto-release.yml` and `prepare-release.yml` were pushing directly to main, which violates these rules. There are no bypass actors configured on the ruleset.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger a manual `prepare-release` dry run to confirm it still calculates versions correctly
- [ ] After merge, push a commit to main to trigger CI -> auto-release flow and verify the PR gets created with auto-merge enabled

author: copilot
body:
Next.js 15 changed `params` in page components to be asynchronous (`Promise`). Three dynamic route client components were either using the old synchronous type or unwrapping via `useEffect`+`.then()`, causing Vercel build type errors.

### Changes

- **`app/messages/[chatId]/page.tsx`** — `params` type was still synchronous `{ chatId: string }`. Updated to `Promise<>` and unwrap with `use()`.
- **`app/checkout/[listingId]/page.tsx`** — Already typed as `Promise<>` but used `useEffect`+`.then()`+`useState` to unwrap. Replaced with `use()`.
- **`app/transactions/escrow/[transactionId]/page.tsx`** — Same `useEffect`+`.then()` pattern, replaced with `use()`.

All three are client components (`"use client"`), so `async`/`await` is not an option. The correct pattern is React's `use()` hook:

```tsx
import { use } from 'react'

export default function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = use(params)
  // ...
}
```

`use()` suspends the component until the promise resolves, handled by Next.js's built-in page Suspense boundary.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> My Vercel build failed with the following Type Error in my dynamic routes:
> `Type error: Type '{ params: { chatId: string; }; }' does not satisfy the constraint 'PageProps'. Types of property 'params' are incompatible. Type '{ chatId: string; }' is missing the following properties from type 'Promise<any>'`
> 
> I am using Next.js 15. In Next.js 15, `params` and `searchParams` passed to pages are asynchronous and must be typed as Promises.
> 
> Please refactor the following dynamic route components to handle Next.js 15 asynchronous params:
> - `app/messages/[chatId]/page.tsx`
> - `app/checkout/[listingId]/page.tsx`
> - `app/transactions/escrow/[transactionId]/page.tsx`
> 
> **Strict Requirements for the Fix:**
> 1. Update the TypeScript interfaces so `params` is a Promise (e.g., `params: Promise<{ chatId: string }>`).
> 2. For Client Components (`"use client"`), you CANNOT make the component async. You MUST import `use` from `react` and unwrap the promise like this:
>    `const { chatId } = use(params);`
> 3. For Server Components, you can make the component `async` and use `const { chatId } = await params;`
> 
> Please provide the updated, corrected code for these specific files.


</details>
