body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **3.0.4** to **7.4.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.2
   ```
   -------------------

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed ``RuntimeError: pipeline must always return at least one result``
  on ~2% of all possible two-byte inputs (e.g. ``b"\xf9\x92"``).
  Multi-byte encodings like CP932 and Johab could score above the
  structural confidence threshold on very short inputs, but then
  statistical scoring would return nothing, leaving the pipeline with an
  empty result list instead of falling through to the ``no_match_encoding``
  fallback.
  (`Jason Barnett <https://github.com/jasonwbarnett>`_ via Claude,
  `367 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/367>`_,
  `368 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/368>`_)

**Improvements:**

- Added ~90 encoding aliases from the WHATWG Encoding Standard and IANA
  Character Sets registry so that ``<meta charset>`` labels like
  ``x-cp1252``, ``x-sjis``, ``dos-874``, ``csUTF8``, and the
  ``cswindows*`` family all resolve correctly through the markup detection
  stage. Every alias was driven by a failing spec-compliance test.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `366 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/366>`_)
- Added a spec-compliance test suite covering Python decode round-trips
  for all 86 registry encodings, WHATWG web-platform label resolution,
  IANA preferred MIME names, and Unicode/RFC conformance (BOM sniffing,
  UTF-8 boundary cases, UTF-16 surrogate pairs). This is the test suite
  that would have caught the 7.4.1 BOM bug before release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `366 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/366>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.4.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bug Fixes:**

- BOM-prefixed UTF-16 and UTF-32 input now reports ``utf-16`` and
  ``utf-32`` instead of the endian-specific variants. Python's
  ``utf-16-le``/``utf-16-be``/``utf-32-le``/``utf-32-be`` codecs keep
  the BOM as a U+FEFF in the decoded string, while ``utf-16``/``utf-32``
  strip it, so callers passing the detection result directly to
  ``.decode()`` were getting a stray BOM at the start of their text.
  BOM-less UTF-16/32 detection (via null-byte patterns) is unchanged
  and still returns the endian-specific name.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `364 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/364>`_,
  `365 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/365>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Performance:**

- Switched to dense zlib-compressed model format (v2): models are now
  stored as contiguous ``memoryview`` slices of a single decompressed
  blob, eliminating per-model ``struct.unpack`` overhead. Cold start
  (import + first detect) dropped from ~75ms to ~13ms with mypyc.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `354 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/354>`_)

**Accuracy:**

- Accuracy improved from 98.6% to 99.3% (2499/2517 files) through
  a combination of training and scoring improvements:

  - Eliminated train/test data overlap by content-fingerprinting test
    suite articles and excluding them from training data
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Added MADLAD-400 and Wikipedia as supplemental training sources to
    fill gaps left by exclusion filtering
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Improved non-ASCII bigram scoring: high-byte bigrams are now
    preserved during training (instead of being crushed by global
    normalization), and weighted by per-bigram IDF so encoding-specific
    byte patterns contribute proportionally to how discriminative they
    are (`352 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/352>`_)
  - Added encoding-aware substitution filtering: character substitutions
    during training now only apply for characters the target encoding
    cannot represent
  - Increased training samples from 15K to 25K per language/encoding pair
    (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Added dedicated structural analyzers for CP932, CP949, and
  Big5-HKSCS: these superset encodings previously shared their base
  encoding's byte-range analyzer, missing extended ranges unique to each
  superset
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `353 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/353>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

**License:**

- **0BSD license** — the project license has been changed from MIT to
  `0BSD <https://opensource.org/license/0bsd>`_, a maximally permissive
  license with no attribution requirement. All prior 7.x releases
  should also be considered 0BSD licensed as of this release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Features:**

- Added ``mime_type`` field to detection results — identifies file types
  for both binary (via magic number matching) and text content. Returned
  in all ``detect()``, ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector`` results.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)
- New ``pipeline/magic.py`` module detects 40+ binary file formats
  including images, audio/video, archives, documents, executables, and
  fonts. ZIP-based formats (XLSX, DOCX, JAR, APK, EPUB, wheel,
  OpenDocument) are distinguished by entry filenames.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed incorrect equivalence between UTF-16-LE and UTF-16-BE in
  accuracy testing — these are distinct encodings with different byte
  order, not interchangeable
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Performance:**

- Added 4 new modules to mypyc compilation (orchestrator, confusion,
  magic, ascii), bringing the total to 11 compiled modules
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Capped statistical scoring at 16 KB — bigram models converge quickly,
  so large files no longer score the full 200 KB. Worst-case detection
  time dropped from 62ms to 26ms with no accuracy loss.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Replaced ``dataclasses.replace()`` with direct ``DetectionResult``
  construction on hot paths, eliminating ~354k function calls per full
  test suite run
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Build:**

- Added riscv64 to the mypyc wheel build matrix — prebuilt wheels are
  now published for RISC-V Linux alongside existing architectures
  (`Bruno Verachten <https://github.com/gounthar>`_,
  `348 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/348>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added ``include_encodings`` and ``exclude_encodings`` parameters to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — restrict or exclude specific
  encodings from the candidate set, with corresponding
  ``-i``/``--include-encodings`` and ``-x``/``--exclude-encodings``
  CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``no_match_encoding`` (default ``"cp1252"``) and
  ``empty_input_encoding`` (default ``"utf-8"``) parameters — control
  which encoding is returned when no candidate survives the pipeline or
  the input is empty, with corresponding CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,

<!-- MANDATORY -->
## Summary
<!-- Provide detailed PR description below -->
This PR aligns the tools workspace with the website integration model by replacing the local shared UI package with `@logto/website-ui-foundation` and moving tool i18n ownership back to the host app. It also hardens the JWT decoder’s JSON editor so syntax highlighting no longer depends on Prism globals when consumed from external hosts.

### Updates
1. Refactor shared UI usage to adopt `@logto/website-ui-foundation`
- Replaced `@logto/tools-components` usage across the dev app and JWT decoder.
- Removed the now-redundant `packages/components` package from the workspace.
- Kept tool-specific composition and styles inside the tool package while relying on the shared website foundation for reusable UI primitives.

2. Restructure tool i18n around a host-owned bridge
- Changed the JWT decoder integration model so the host app owns the real i18n provider and passes resolved i18n methods into the tool.
- Exported JWT decoder locale resources from the tool package as the source of truth for host-side merging.
- Added reusable adapter/resource helpers in `@logto/tools-i18nova` to support this host-first integration pattern.
- Updated the dev app to merge tool resources into its own i18n store and pass a typed i18n bridge into `JwtDecoder`.

3. Improve JWT decoder embedding reliability
- Removed the dependency on Prism’s JSON side-effect module, which expects a global `Prism`.
- Inlined the JSON grammar used by the editor so syntax highlighting works reliably in ESM/workspace-hosted builds.

4. Clean up workspace/package wiring
- Updated package dependencies to reflect the new UI foundation and local workspace linkage for `@logto/tools-i18nova`.
- Refreshed README guidance so it documents the new host-first i18n contract and shared UI direction.

### Impact

- Establishes the intended integration pattern for future tools: host-owned i18n, tool-exported resources, and shared website UI primitives.
- Simplifies the workspace by removing a duplicated internal component layer.
- Reduces embedding risk for JWT decoder consumers, especially in website-style bundled environments.

author: copilot
body:
Implements a production-ready, configuration-driven submission platform supporting multiple services, journey types, and UK public sector design system themes — built on Node.js/Express with a vanilla JS SPA frontend.

## Core layers

- **Service registry** — auto-discovers services from `services/` directory, validates against JSON schema
- **Journey provider** — `LocalJsonProvider` reads service JSON config; `DataverseProvider` stub ready for future integration
- **Theme system** — adapter-per-theme (GDS base + MoJ, DWP, HMRC, selfDefined variants); variant resolution, unsupported-component fallback with dev warning
- **Renderer** — server-side HTML generation via template literals (no Nunjucks); WCAG 2.2 AA: `fieldset`/`legend`, `aria-describedby`, error summary with field links
- **Validation engine** — data-driven: `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `numeric`, `date`
- **Branching engine** — data-driven operators: `equals`, `notEquals`, `contains`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan`, `in`
- **Task list engine** — dependency resolution, status lifecycle (`notStarted` → `inProgress` → `completed`, `cannotStartYet`), required-task gate before submission
- **State store** — in-memory, isolated per `serviceId` + `submissionId`
- **Security middleware** — Helmet + strict CSP, rate limiting (100 req/15 min), `Permissions-Policy`, no `X-Powered-By`
- **SPA shell** — vanilla JS + `history.pushState`, focus management on navigation, page title updates

## Example services

| Service | Journey type | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| Apply for a juggling licence | `simpleLinear` | GDS |
| Report a lost visitor pass | `taskList` | MoJ (extends GDS) |

## API surface

```
GET  /api/services
GET  /api/services/:id
GET  /api/services/:id/journey
POST /api/services/:id/session/start
GET  /api/services/:id/session/:sid/state
POST /api/services/:id/session/:sid/answers
POST /api/services/:id/session/:sid/submit
GET  /api/services/:id/session/:sid/validate/:pageId
GET  /api/themes/:themeKey
```

## Tests

38 tests across 7 suites: schema validation, theme resolution, validation engine, branching engine, task list logic, security headers, and service state isolation.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# MASTER COPILOT PROMPT

## Multi-Service GDS Submission Platform (Production Ready)

You are an expert full stack engineer specialising in secure, accessible, multi-service submission platforms built with Node.js.

This is NOT a prototype.
This is a reusable submission platform that must support multiple services, multiple journey types, multiple themes, and future Dataverse-backed configuration.

---

## 1. Core Objective

Build a Node.js-based submission platform that:

* supports multiple services in one application
* supports multiple journey types:

  * simpleLinear
  * taskList
* supports multiple UK public sector design systems via a theme layer
* is fully accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA)
* is secure by default
* is fully configuration driven
* is designed to later load configuration from Dataverse

---

## 2. Technology Stack

* Node.js
* Express (server)
* Vite + vanilla JavaScript (SPA frontend)
* GOV.UK Frontend (where applicable)

Do not use Nunjucks.
Do not use React unless absolutely necessary.

---

## 3. Platform Architecture

Structure the system into clear layers:

* platform shell
* service registry
* journey provider (JSON now, Dataverse later)
* theme provider
* renderer
* router
* validation engine
* branching engine
* state store
* security middleware

Key rule:
Do not mix concerns between layers.

---

## 4. Multi-Service Support

The platform must support multiple services.

Create at least two:

1. Apply for a juggling licence (simpleLinear)
2. Report a lost visitor pass (taskList)

Each service must have:

* serviceId
* name
* description
* journeyType
* theme configuration
* journey definition
* version information

Add a service registry and a landing page listing all services.

State must be isolated per service and per submission.

---

## 5. Journey Types

### simpleLinear

* page-by-page navigation
* ends with check answers page
* then confirmation page

### taskList

* multi-section journey
* includes a task list page
* tasks grouped into sections
* task statuses:

  * notStarted
  * inProgress
  * completed
  * cannotStartYet
* conditional task unlocking
* user can return to task list
* must complete required tasks before submission
* ends with check answers page

The system must support both journey types using the same core engine.

---

## 6. Data-Driven Journey Model

All journeys must be driven from configuration.

Do NOT hard code pages.

The schema must support:

* service metadata
* journeyType
* routes
* pages
* questions
* options
* validation rules
* branching rules
* task groups
* tasks
* check answers configuration
* confirmation content

Define a clear schema before implementation.

Include schemaVersion.

Treat JSON as configuration only, never executable logic.

---

## 7. Theme System (Critical)

Each service must define its theme at the top of its configuration.

### Theme Model

Support:

* baseTheme
* variantTheme (optional)

Example:

* baseTheme: gds
* variantTheme: dwp

### Supported Themes

Base:

* gds: https://design-system.service.gov.uk/

Variants:

* moj: https://design-patterns.service.justice.gov.uk/
* mod: https://design-system.service.mod.gov.uk/
* nhs: https://service-manual.nhs.uk/design-system
* ons: https://service-manual.ons.gov.uk/design-system
* hmrc: https://design.tax.service.gov.uk/
* dwp: https://design-system.dwp.gov.uk/

Custom:

* selfDefined
* exampleTheme

### Theme Requirements

* Themes must be implemented as adapters
* Variant themes may extend base themes
* MOJ, HMRC, DWP extend GOV.UK where appropriate
* Renderer must NOT contain theme-specific logic

Each theme must define:

* theme key
* display name
* base theme
* source URL
* supported components
* overridden components
* fallback strategy
* styling hooks

If a component is unsupported:

* use fallback
* log warning in development

---

## 8. Accessibility Requirements

Must meet WCAG 2.2 AA:

* semantic HTML
* proper labels for all inputs
* fieldset + legend for grouped inputs
* aria-describedby for hints and errors
* error summary linked to fields
* keyboard navigation support
* focus management on navigation and errors
* update page title on route change

---

## 9. Security Requirements

### Server Side

* Use Helmet
* Strict Content Security Policy
* X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
* Referrer-Policy set
* Permissions-Policy set
* Prevent clickjacking
* Disable x-powered-by
* Rate limiting
* Safe static file serving
* No stack traces exposed

### Client Side

* No eval or dynamic code execution
* Escape all rendered content
* Prevent XSS via configuration
* Prevent open redirects
* Treat all config as untrusted input

### Storage

* Minimise stored data
* Use memory or sessionStorage
* Do not store sensitive data unnecessarily

---

## 10. Dataverse-Ready Architecture

Design the system so configuration can later be stored in Dataverse.

Model configuration as:

* services
* journey versions
* pages
* questions
* options
* tasks
* task groups
* branching rules
* val...

</details>

### Motivation
- Umożliwić szybką ocenę jakości śledzenia poprzez wyliczane sekcje trendów (utrata śladu, stabilność, confidence) dodane do raportów metryk.
- Zdefiniować jednolity, offline-analizowalny format logów diagnostycznych, aby ułatwić agregację i debug poza środowiskiem real-time.
- Eksportować skondensowane podsumowania per sesja i prosty dashboard QA, oraz powiązać sesyjne raporty z wynikami benchmarku regresji.

### Description
- Dodano kontrakt pól `DIAGNOSTIC_LOG_FIELDS` oraz funkcje diagnostyczne w `packages/luca-reporting/src/luca_reporting/reports.py`: `build_quality_trend_sections`, `_normalize_diagnostic_event`, `save_diagnostic_log`, `build_session_summary`, `save_session_summary_csv`, `save_session_summary_json`, `link_regression_benchmark` oraz `build_qa_dashboard_markdown` i pomocnicze utilsy.\n
- Wzbogacono profile metryk (`PROFILE_METRICS`) i automatycznie włączono sekcje trendów do wyniku `metrics_from_points_with_profile` (zwracane metryki zawierają teraz pola `trend_*`).
- Rozszerzono publiczne API pakietu `luca-reporting` (`__init__.py`) oraz zaktualizowano `README.md` i `CHANGELOG.md` o nowe funkcje i kontrakt diagnostyczny.
- Podłączono eksport artefaktów QA do pipeline trackingu w `packages/luca-tracking/src/luca_tracking/pipeline.py` poprzez funkcję `_export_session_quality_artifacts`, która generuje: `*_session_summary.csv`, `*_session_summary.json`, `*_qa_dashboard.md` oraz `*_diagnostics.jsonl`; dodano też mechanizm best-effort łączenia z `benchmark_delta.csv` przez `link_regression_benchmark`.

### Testing
- Uruchomiono kompilację plików Python: `python -m compileall packages/luca-reporting/src packages/luca-tracking/src` (PASS).

## Summary

- Wraps 8 additional read-only `amz_scout.api` functions as Chainlit tools on top of Phase 1's `query_latest`, bringing the webapp to the full 9-tool query surface: `check_freshness`, `keepa_budget`, `query_availability`, `query_compare`, `query_deals`, `query_ranking`, `query_sellers`, `query_trends`.
- Each schema carries bilingual CN/EN descriptions matching `CLAUDE.md`'s decision-tree phrases (价格趋势 / 对比 / 排名 / 上架 / 卖家 / 促销 / 数据多久没更新了 / Keepa token), so Sonnet 4.6 routes Chinese queries correctly without a SYSTEM_PROMPT enumeration.
- Moves `cache_control` from `query_latest` to `query_trends` (the new last/most-called tool) so all 9 tool definitions sit in a single prompt-cache breakpoint.
- Purely additive: **zero changes to `app.py`, `llm.py`, `auth.py`, `config.py`, or `amz_scout/`.**

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `webapp/tools.py` | +309 / -4 — 8 new tool schemas, 8 `@cl.step` wrappers, 8 dispatcher branches, `cache_control` move |
| `tests/test_webapp_smoke.py` | +77 — 2 new tests (exact name set + dispatcher routing through every wrapper) |
| `.claude/PRPs/prds/internal-amz-scout-web.prd.md` | Phase 2 status → `complete`, plan link → `completed/` |
| `.claude/PRPs/plans/completed/phase2-query-tools.plan.md` | Archived |
| `.claude/PRPs/reports/phase2-query-tools-report.md` | New implementation report (deviations, validation, acceptance) |

## Deviations from plan

Documented in full in the report, but the three worth flagging at review time:

1. **Import style** — `ruff` isort (I001) didn't accept the plan's grouped multi-line `from amz_scout.api import (...)` block, so I switched to 9 single-line aliased imports. Purely cosmetic.
2. **Dispatcher routing test required two layers of monkeypatching** — `@cl.step` raises `ChainlitContextException` outside an active Chainlit session, and with a real `amz_scout.db` present a raw `_api_query_trends` call would attempt a Keepa network fetch (and hang). Fix: monkeypatch `cl.step` to a no-op decorator *before* re-importing `webapp.tools`, plus stub every `webapp.tools._api_*` alias with a fake envelope. The test is now ~0.5s and exercises every wrapper's call path. See `tests/test_webapp_smoke.py::test_dispatcher_routes_all_known_tools`.
3. **Manual browser validation moved out-of-pass, then done interactively in the session** — see test plan below; three representative queries were confirmed live with screenshots.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check webapp/ tests/test_webapp_smoke.py` | ✅ zero issues |
| `ruff format --check` | ✅ all files already formatted |
| `pytest tests/test_webapp_smoke.py -v` | ✅ 6/6 (1.60s) |
| `pytest -q` (full suite) | ✅ 226/226 (35.25s), zero regressions |
| Import surface | ✅ `TOOL_SCHEMAS` has the exact 9 expected names |

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean
- [x] `pytest tests/test_webapp_smoke.py -v` — 6 tests pass
- [x] `pytest -q` — 226 tests pass, zero regressions
- [x] Live Chinese query: `"Keepa 还有多少 token"` → renders `keepa_budget` step, returns 57/60 tokens in a bilingual table
- [x] Live Chinese query: `"列出所有产品在哪些市场上有卖"` → renders `query_availability` step, gracefully surfaces empty-state hint (`amz_scout scrape`)
- [x] Live Chinese query: `"GL-Slate 7 在英国过去 6 个月的价格趋势"` → renders `query_trends` (called twice for multi-series), surfaces `meta.warnings` for fuzzy product match (`Slate 7` → `GL-BE3600 / B0F2MR53D6`), displays real GBP time series
- [x] `cache_control` on `query_trends` only (enforced by `test_tool_schemas_have_cache_control_on_last`)

## Notes for reviewers

- Only the last tool in `TOOL_SCHEMAS` has `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` — this is intentional and load-bearing for prompt caching. The smoke test enforces it, so don't "helpfully" add it to other tools.
- The dispatcher uses independent `if`/`return` branches instead of `elif` — keeps diffs minimal when Phase 3/4 add more tools.
- All `args.get(key, default)` — never `args[key]`. LLMs occasionally drop fields from tool calls, and we want envelope-shaped errors, not `KeyError` crashes.
- The webapp LLM does **not** auto-backfill missing product data via WebSearch. That's Claude Code's job (CLAUDE.md rule 12), and the DB is the shared channel between the two runtimes. The webapp surfaces `meta.new_product=True` to the user and stops there. This split is deliberate and was confirmed in live testing.

Closes Phase 2 of [internal-amz-scout-web.prd.md](.claude/PRPs/prds/internal-amz-scout-web.prd.md).

author: serdun
body:
## Problem

When a user starts an outgoing call with no network, the call was automatically hung up ~300ms after the first `SignalingConnectionFailed` event — before the reconnect controller had any chance to retry.

**Root cause** (`call_bloc.dart` — `__onCallPerformEventStarted`):

```dart
final signalingFailed = next.callServiceState.signalingClientStatus.isFailure;
return signalingReady || signalingFailed;  // exits on first failure
```

`signalingFailed` short-circuited the `firstWhere` on the very first connection attempt failure, bypassing `kSignalingClientConnectionTimeout` entirely and immediately calling `callkeep.endCall()`.

**Expected behaviour:** call stays in DIALING state for up to 30 seconds while the reconnect controller retries; only ends if still no connection after the timeout (or user presses hangup).

## Fix

- Removed `signalingFailed` from the `firstWhere` predicate — it now only exits on `signalingReady` or timeout.
- Added `kOutgoingCallSignalingWaitTimeout = Duration(seconds: 30)` used exclusively for this in-call wait. The existing `kSignalingClientConnectionTimeout` (10s) is unchanged and still used for the pre-call wait in `_continueStartCallIntent`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Start an outgoing call with airplane mode on — call stays on screen for 30s, then ends with "Call while offline" notification
- [ ] Start an outgoing call with airplane mode on, restore network within 30s — call proceeds normally
- [ ] Normal outgoing call (network available) — no regression, call goes through immediately

## Summary

When a CLI model hits a rate limit (e.g. codex-spark exhausts quota), aimux automatically
retries with the next model in the profile's fallback chain before switching CLI entirely.

### What's new

- **Error classification** — `ClassifyError(content, stderr, exitCode)` returns Quota/Transient/Fatal
- **Model cooldown tracker** — per-(cli,model) cooldown prevents re-trying rate-limited models
- **Profile-level model_fallback** — ordered model list in CLI profile YAML
- **Retry helper** — `runWithModelFallback` used by both `executeJob` and `RunAgent`
- **Three-category error handling:**
  - Quota → model fallback + cooldown (5 min default)
  - Transient → retry same model once, NO cooldown
  - Fatal → skip CLI immediately

### Config example (codex profile)

```yaml
model_fallback:
  - gpt-5.3-codex-spark    # primary (fast, lower quota)
  - gpt-5.3-codex           # fallback (slower, higher quota)
cooldown_seconds: 300
```

### Spec

Full spec + plan + tasks at `.agent/specs/model-fallback-chain/`

## Test plan

- [x] 15 ClassifyError tests (quota/transient/fatal/none patterns)
- [x] 8 ModelCooldownTracker tests (expiry, filter, concurrent, isolation)
- [x] 5 isQuotaError tests (stdout/stderr patterns)
- [x] 5 ModelFallback integration tests (quota→success, all-quota, transient-retry, cooldown-skip, no-config)
- [x] Full `go test ./pkg/... -timeout 300s` — no new failures
- [ ] E2E test deferred (requires testcli emulator rate-limit simulation)

author: copilot
body:
`UsbStorageBlocker` disables `USBSTOR\Start` globally at block time, but the unblock flow did not guarantee the service was restored before per-device flags were cleared or WMI re-enable was attempted — leaving USB storage broken after unblocking. Additionally, if the block record was missing or from a pre-recording version, the user was silently bricked with no guidance.

## `UnblockManager`
- **Action ordering**: actions are now sorted before execution — `ServiceStart` for `usbstor` (priority 0) → other `ServiceStart` (1) → `ConfigFlags` (2) → `WmiDisable` (3). Ensures the global storage driver is live before device re-enumeration.
- **WMI targeting**: `EnableViaWmi` tries an InstanceId-specific query first, falling back to VID/PID wildcard. Avoids enabling the wrong composite interface on multi-interface devices.
- **No-record recovery sentinel**: when `usbstor` has no recorded `PreviousServiceStart`, `RestoreServiceStart` returns a `RECOVERY_REQUIRED:` prefix instead of silently skipping or guessing a default.
- **Device re-enumeration**: `TriggerDeviceRescan()` calls `cfgmgr32!CM_Locate_DevNodeW` + `CM_Reenumerate_DevNode` after all restore steps, so Windows rediscovers the device without a manual unplug/replug.
- **WQL injection prevention**: `SanitizeWqlLike()` escapes `%`, `_`, `[` in InstanceId/VID/PID before embedding in WMI queries. Switched to `CM_Locate_DevNodeW` (Unicode) with named constants (`CR_SUCCESS`, `CM_LOCATE_DEVNODE_NORMAL`, `CM_REENUMERATE_NORMAL`).

## `UnblockDevicesForm`
- **Global storage warning**: if the selected record contains a `ServiceStart` action for `usbstor`, a prominent dialog fires before confirmation explaining the system-wide impact.
- **Recovery dialog**: after unblock, any `RECOVERY_REQUIRED:` result triggers a step-by-step manual restoration dialog (regedit path + correct `Start` value).

## `Program` — startup orphan detection
- `CheckOrphanedUsbStorDisable()` runs at startup: if `USBSTOR\Start == 4` but no `BlockedDeviceRecord` contains a matching `ServiceStart` action, logs a critical event and shows a tray balloon. Prevents silent brick from pre-recording-era blocks or lost records.

```csharp
// Ordering example — before this fix, ServiceStart ran wherever it appeared in the list
var orderedActions = record.Actions
    .OrderBy(a =>
    {
        if (a.ActionType == "ServiceStart" &&
            string.Equals(a.ServiceName, "usbstor", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return 0;
        if (a.ActionType == "ServiceStart") return 1;
        if (a.ActionType == "ConfigFlags")  return 2;
        if (a.ActionType == "WmiDisable")   return 3;
        return 4;
    })
    .ToList();
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Urgent fix in `Terrible24-USB/USB-Guardian`: the app disabled USB storage globally by setting `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\USBSTOR\Start = 4` (as evidenced by user screenshot). The current unblock flow did not restore the global `USBSTOR` Start value reliably, causing storage to remain broken after unblocking.

Implement a safety-critical restoration and unblock logic update:

1) **Immediate restoration logic**:
   - Add an explicit unblocking path that restores `Services\USBSTOR\Start` if it is currently 4 and USB Guardian previously set it.
   - Ensure restore uses the **previous value recorded at block time** (no hardcoded defaults). If no previous value exists in the blocked record, do NOT guess; instead show a clear warning and provide a controlled recovery prompt explaining the risk and asking the user to restore to Windows default manually.

2) **Guarantee recording of USBSTOR Start changes**:
   - In `UsbStorageBlocker.SetPermanentBlockFlags`, when setting `usbstor\Start` to 4, ensure it always records a `BlockActionRecord` of type `ServiceStart` with `ServiceName="usbstor"` and `PreviousServiceStart` set to the current value before changing it.
   - Ensure this record is persisted to `blocked_devices.json` via `BlockedDeviceStore` for every storage block.

3) **Unblock ordering**:
   - When unblocking a storage device, restore `usbstor` Start **before** attempting WMI enable and before clearing ConfigFlags, or in a robust order that ensures the system can re-enumerate immediately.
   - After restoration, trigger a re-enumeration step if feasible (e.g., prompt user to unplug/replug; optionally call a device rescan via SetupAPI/Devcon-style, if safe and implementable).

4) **WMI enable targeting**:
   - Improve `UnblockManager.EnableViaWmi` to target a more specific device if possible (use instance id / PNPDeviceID match), not only VID/PID wildcard.

5) **Add a recovery UI warning**:
   - In `UnblockDevicesForm`, if the selected record contains a `ServiceStart` action for `usbstor`, display a prominent warning that unblocking will restore USB storage globally.

6) **Regression protection**:
   - Add a self-check at startup: if `USBSTOR\Start==4` but there are *no* blocked device records indicating USB Guardian disabled it, log a critical warning and surface a notification so the user is not silently bricked.

7) Keep safety constraints:
   - Do not restore any service start value unless it was recorded.
   - Do not perform destructive actions in dry-run mode.

Create a PR against `master` in `Terrible24-USB/USB-Guardian` with these fixes.

Context evidence:
- User screenshot shows `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\USBSTOR\Start = 4`.
- Code currently disables USBSTOR in `UsbStorageBlocker.SetPermanentBlockFlags`.
- Unblock manager restores based on recorded actions; the issue is that restoration isn't happening or the record isn't present/ordered.


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: now let's move on to code what are the improvements to be made first is the unblock feature others are 

Assistant: Top priority improvements (in order) should be:

## 1) **Unblock feature (recovery) — do this first**
Right now blocking can involve **multiple mechanisms**, so unblocking must reverse the same ones safely and predictably.

### What “blocked” means in your code today
Blocking can happen via:
1) **Registry:** `ConfigFlags |= 0x100` (disabled) on  
   `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USB\VID_xxxx&PID_yyyy\<InstanceId>`
2) **WMI:** `Win32_PnPEntity.InvokeMethod("Disable")`
3) **Storage-specific extra hardening:** in `UsbStorageBlocker.SetPermanentBlockFlags()`:
   - `ConfigFlags |= 0x100 | 0x40` (disable + reinstall prevention)
   - `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\usbstor\Start = 4` (disables USB storage driver globally)

So unblocking must handle all 3, and must **not accidentally re-enable the wrong device**.

### Improvements to implement for unblocking
**A. Add a persistent “blocked devices” registry/database**
- Create `blocked_devices.json` storing at least:
  - `Vid`, `Pid`, `InstanceId`, `SerialNumber`, `FingerprintHash`
  - `BlockReason`
  - `BlockMethodsUsed`: `[WMI, ConfigFlags, UsbStorService]`
  - Timestamp
This prevents guessing later.

**B. Implement `UnblockDevice(DeviceFingerprint device)` in `UsbBlockingManager`**
Minimum reversible steps:
- Remove the disabled bit from ConfigFlags:
  - `ConfigFlags = ConfigFlags & ~0x100`
- Also remove reinstall bit if you set it:
  - `ConfigFlags = ConfigFlags & ~0x40`
- Re-enable via WMI:
  - `InvokeMethod("Enable")`
- If you disabled the device’s service start value:
  - restore it (but only if you previously changed it and recorded the old value)

**C. Storage-specific: fix the “global usbstor disable” risk**
Right now you disable `usbstor` globally, which can break *all* USB storage.
For unblocking:
- restore `Services\usbstor\Start` to a sane default...

</details>

author: mugen87
body:
Fixed #10706.

**Description**

Another attempt to fix #10706. I've realized there is a much cleaner approach to fix the race condition in `AudioLoader` that potentially occurs when used with `LoadingManager`. 

To recap: `LoadingManager` can fire too early when the audio isn't decoded yet so if you attempt to playback such an audio you run into runtime errors. However, by using a separate "decode item", it's possible to keep the `LoadingManager` waiting until the decode has finished.

This change requires no changes in `FileLoader` which was a blocker of previous PRs.

body:
## Summary
Introduces a complete Nifty 50 stock monitoring system that tracks intraday price movements and fetches relevant news articles when stocks move beyond a configurable threshold (default ±5%).

## Key Changes

- **Price Monitoring (`monitor/price_checker.py`)**: 
  - Fetches previous close prices from yfinance and compares against current intraday prices
  - Detects stocks moving ±N% and returns detailed alerts with symbol, company name, and percentage change
  - Handles single and multi-ticker yfinance responses gracefully

- **Nifty 50 Constituent List (`monitor/nifty50.py`)**:
  - Fetches official NSE Nifty 50 constituent list from CSV endpoint
  - Implements local JSON cache with 7-day TTL to reduce API calls
  - Falls back to hardcoded list of 50 stocks (as of early 2026) if NSE fetch fails

- **News Fetching (`monitor/news_fetcher.py`)**:
  - Searches Google News RSS for articles related to stock moves
  - Parses RSS 2.0 XML using stdlib `xml.etree.ElementTree` (no external feed parser)
  - Formats alerts with news articles, sources, and publication dates
  - Implements polite 2-second delay between requests

- **Scheduling (`monitor/scheduler.py`)**:
  - Uses APScheduler to run price checks every 15 minutes (configurable) during market hours
  - Runs intraday checks Mon-Fri between 9:15 AM – 3:30 PM IST
  - Executes end-of-day summary at market close (3:30 PM)
  - Handles graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM

- **Configuration & Logging**:
  - Centralized config (`monitor/config.py`) with environment variable overrides
  - Dual-output logger: INFO+ to stdout, DEBUG+ to daily rotating log files
  - Example `.env` file for optional configuration

- **Entry Point (`main.py`)**:
  - Orchestrates startup: loads Nifty 50 list, initializes price checker, starts scheduler
  - Logs configuration and stock count at startup

## Implementation Details

- **yfinance Integration**: Converts NSE symbols to Yahoo Finance format (appends `.NS`), handles special characters (e.g., `&` removal)
- **Previous Close Logic**: Uses second-to-last row from 5-day historical data as previous close; falls back to last available if only 1 day exists
- **Error Resilience**: Graceful exception handling throughout; missing data for individual stocks doesn't block others
- **Market Hours**: Hardcoded to IST (Asia/Kolkata) with configurable check interval and threshold

author: arnoldwender
body:
## Problem

`add_triple()` uses a SELECT-then-INSERT pattern with no database-level uniqueness guarantee — a classic TOCTOU race. Two concurrent callers can both execute the SELECT (both see no existing row), then both proceed to INSERT, producing duplicate active triples.

The existing `INSERT OR IGNORE` did not help because the `id` column is generated with `datetime.now().isoformat()` baked in — every call produces a unique primary key, so `INSERT OR IGNORE` never triggers.

There is also no `UNIQUE` constraint on `(subject, predicate, object) WHERE valid_to IS NULL`, so the database cannot enforce the invariant independently of Python logic.

Fixes #655.

## Solution

**1. Partial UNIQUE index** (`_init_db`):
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_triples_active
    ON triples(subject, predicate, object)
    WHERE valid_to IS NULL;
```
This is the database-level enforcement layer — no concurrent caller can bypass it.

**2. Dedup migration** (also `_init_db`):
Before creating the index, remove any pre-existing duplicate active triples (keeping the oldest by `rowid`) so the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` does not fail on upgraded databases.

**3. Deterministic ID for active triples** (`add_triple`):
Active triples use `id_seed = f"{sub_id}|{pred}|{obj_id}|active"` so the computed `triple_id` is the same for both concurrent callers. `INSERT OR IGNORE` then discards the second insert atomically. Expired triples retain the `datetime.now()` component so re-adds after invalidation always generate a distinct row.

**4. Atomic upsert pattern**:
Replace SELECT-check + plain INSERT with INSERT OR IGNORE followed by a SELECT to return whichever row won (ours or a concurrent insert's).

## Test results

All existing `test_knowledge_graph.py` tests pass, including `test_duplicate_triple_returns_existing_id` and `test_invalidated_triple_allows_re_add`.

author: alexkibler
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in `api/Controllers/SessionsController.cs`. The endpoints for getting, updating, and deleting sessions relied solely on the provided session ID without verifying that the session belonged to the authenticated user. Furthermore, the `DeleteSession` endpoint used an insecure anti-pattern by manually extracting and parsing the JWT from the `Authorization` header instead of using the built-in ASP.NET Core authorization pipeline.
🎯 **Impact:** Any authenticated user could view, modify, or delete any other user's game sessions by simply knowing or guessing the session UUID.
🔧 **Fix:** 
1. Added the `[Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.Authorize]` attribute to the vulnerable endpoints.
2. Extracted the authenticated user's ID securely using standard middleware: `User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)`.
3. Verified ownership by comparing `session.UserId` against the requesting user's `userId`, returning a `403 Forbidden` response if they do not match.
4. Cleaned up the `DeleteSession` endpoint to remove the manual token parsing anti-pattern.
✅ **Verification:** 
1. `cd api.Tests && dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` completes successfully (17/17 tests passing), ensuring no regressions.
2. Analyzed endpoint logic to ensure it now appropriately leverages ASP.NET core authorization boundaries.

body:
## Bakgrunn

Gjennomgang av personvernhåndtering avdekket fire kritiske funn (P1) som kan eksponere fødselsnummer i logger, heap-dumps og HTTP-responser, samt sende data for skjermede personer til BigQuery ved PDL-nedetid.

## Endringer

### 1. Hash cache-nøkkel i PDL-cache (`PdlGateway.kt`)
FNR ble lagret som ren tekst som cache-nøkkel i Caffeine-cachen, og kunne dukke opp i heap-dumps og GC-logging. Nøkkelen hashes nå med SHA-256.

### 2. Fjern FNR fra exception-melding (`PdlGateway.kt`)
`requireNotNull` kastet en exception med FNR i meldingen. Erstattet med `"(ident maskert)"`.

### 3. Kast exception ved PDL-nedetid (`SkjermingService.kt`)
Ved `HttpConnectTimeoutException` og `ConnectException` returnerte tjenesten `false` (ikke skjermet), noe som kunne sende en skjermet persons data til BigQuery. Kaster nå exception slik at jobben feiler og kan kjøres på nytt.

### 4. Fjern exception-innhold fra HTTP 500-respons (`App.kt`)
`$cause` i feilresponsen kunne inneholde FNR fra exception-meldingen i punkt 2. Returnerer nå generisk `"500: Internal Server Error"`.

author: mdmanurung
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a complete consensus matrix factorization pipeline to MOFA-FLEX, porting the consensus NMF principles from the cNMF package to the multi-view setting. The implementation enables robust factor discovery by running multiple independent fits, pooling results, and building consensus factors through density-based filtering and k-means clustering.

## Key Changes

- **New module `mofaflex/tl/_consensus.py`**: Implements the full consensus pipeline with ~970 lines of code including:
  - `fit_consensus()`: Main entry point that orchestrates multiple MOFA-FLEX fits with distinct seeds, pools weight spectra across runs, filters outliers via local density, clusters survivors with k-means, computes per-cluster median consensus weights, and refits factor matrices via non-negative least squares
  - `k_selection()`: Sweeps consensus fits across multiple factor counts to aid k selection
  - `ConsensusResult`: Dataclass holding consensus weights, factors, stability metrics, reconstruction error, and diagnostic information
  - `KSelectionResult`: Aggregates results across k values with plotting utilities
  - Internal helpers for spectra matrix construction, density filtering, clustering, and refitting

- **Diagnostic and visualization methods**:
  - `ConsensusResult.plot_clustergram()`: Faithful port of cNMF's diagnostic clustergram showing reordered distance matrix, cluster labels, and local density histogram
  - `KSelectionResult.plot()`: plotnine-based k-selection plot
  - `KSelectionResult.plot_cnmf()`: matplotlib twin-axis k-selection plot matching cNMF's style

- **Updated `mofaflex/tl/__init__.py`**: Exports the new public API (`fit_consensus`, `k_selection`, `ConsensusResult`, `KSelectionResult`)

- **Comprehensive test suite `tests/test_consensus.py`**: 
  - Tests for result shapes, stability/error metrics, diagnostic bookkeeping
  - Validation that non-negative constraints are enforced
  - Tests for k-selection sweep and plotting
  - Verification of factor reordering by usage contribution
  - Clustergram and k-selection plot rendering tests

## Implementation Details

- **Fully non-negative only**: The pipeline requires both `nonnegative_factors=True` and `nonnegative_weights=True` on the template, validated early to catch misconfiguration
- **Multi-view consensus**: Extends cNMF's single-view approach by per-view L2-normalizing weight columns before concatenation, ensuring views contribute comparably to distance metrics despite different scales
- **Spectra pooling**: Builds a `(n_runs * k, sum_v n_features[v])` matrix with per-view normalization followed by global L2 normalization
- **Density filtering**: Implements cNMF's local density outlier detection using k-nearest neighbors (k = `local_neighborhood_size * n_runs`)
- **Consensus via median**: Takes element-wise median of L2-normalized spectra per cluster, then splits back into per-view weight matrices
- **NNLS refit**: Uses sklearn's `non_negative_factorization` with `update_H=False` to refit per-group factor matrices against fixed consensus weights, reconciling all views through a single shared factor matrix
- **Factor reordering**: Sorts factors by total usage contribution descending, matching cNMF's convention
- **Deterministic clustering**: KMeans uses `random_state=1` for reproducibility; cluster labels are remapped to contiguous IDs in order of first appearance

# Backport

This will backport the following commits from `main` to `9.3`:
 - [[Securoty Solution] prevent flyout scroll jump when hover actions focus panel (#262682)](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/262682)

<!--- Backport version: 11.0.1 -->

### Questions ?
Please refer to the [Backport tool documentation](https://github.com/sorenlouv/backport)

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Jon Wålstedt","email":"jon.walstedt@elastic.co"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2026-04-13T09:34:33Z","message":"[Securoty Solution] prevent flyout scroll jump when hover actions focus panel (#262682)

## Summary

**Problem:** In **Mozilla Firefox**, scrolling the **Table** tab of the
**alert / document details flyout** (the field/value list) could **jump
to the bottom** after **hovering a row** so the **cell action** strip
appears. The bad scroll often showed up on the **next** scroll gesture,
making long field lists hard to use.

**Cause:** `EuiPopover` uses a focus trap by default. When the hover
menu opens, focus moves into the action panel. The browser then
**scrolls scrollable ancestors** (notably the flyout body) to keep the
focused node in view—here that effectively **yanks** the flyout scroll
position (often to the end of the scrollable area).

**Change:** Set `focusTrapProps={{ preventScrollOnFocus: true }}` on the
`EuiPopover` in `HoverActionsPopover` (`@kbn/cell-actions`). That flows
through `react-focus-on` / `react-focus-lock` as `focus({ preventScroll:
true })` when focus enters the panel, so **ancestor scroll position is
preserved** while keeping normal focus behavior for the actions.

**Scope:** Affects any UI that uses **hover** cell actions
(`CellActionsMode.HOVER_DOWN` / `HOVER_RIGHT`), including the Security
alert flyout **Table** view.

Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/sdh-security-team/issues/1623

**Before**


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbc91261-b178-4296-9116-3eca77dc6970

**After**


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8869d17-4071-4893-9b3b-6fb6d888a772

---

## Release note (for the label / changelog)

> **Security — Alerts:** Fixed Firefox scroll position jumping to the
bottom of the document details flyout **Table** tab after hovering field
rows with cell actions.

---

## Risk

**Overall severity: low.** There are no HTTP, persistence, or
security-control changes; this is a client-side focus/scroll interaction
fix in `@kbn/cell-actions`.

| Area | Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|------|-----------|------------|
| **Scroll / layout** | Suppressing scroll-on-focus fixes the flyout
jump but means the browser **no longer auto-scrolls ancestors** to
reveal the focused node when focus enters the panel. In edge cases (e.g.
panel partly off-screen), the focused control might not be scrolled into
view automatically. | Low | Hover popovers are anchored to the cell and
`repositionOnScroll` updates position; primary bug was ancestor scroll
(flyout body), not missing panel visibility. Smoke-test Firefox +
Chromium on the alert flyout **Table** tab. |
| **Blast radius** | Every consumer of `CellActionsMode.HOVER_DOWN` /
`HOVER_RIGHT` inherits the change (Security flyout, other tables using
hover cell actions). | Low | Same behavior is desirable anywhere a
scroll container wraps the grid/flyout; unintended regressions are
unlikely. |
| **Accessibility** | Focus still moves into the action strip via the
existing focus trap; only **`focus({ preventScroll: true })`** is added.
Screen reader and keyboard users are not losing the trap or labels. |
Low | Optional: tab through actions after hover-open in Firefox to
confirm nothing regressed. |
| **Browser variance** | Issue was most visible in **Firefox**; other
browsers may already have been less aggressive about scrolling
ancestors. | Low | Treat Firefox as the validation target; spot-check
Chrome or Edge. |
| **Performance** | Extra prop only; no new listeners or renders. |
Negligible | None. |

See
[RISK_MATRIX.mdx](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/RISK_MATRIX.mdx)
for how Elastic frames severity in larger PRs; this change does not
warrant escalation beyond routine review.

---

## Checklist — what to tick (this PR)

| Item | Tick? | Notes |
|------|--------|--------|
| EUI writing + i18n | **Yes** | No new user-visible strings; only a
`focusTrapProps` prop and an English **code comment** (not product
copy). |
| Documentation | **Yes** | Bugfix / UX correction; no new feature or
workflow that needs dev docs. |
| Unit or functional tests | **Optional / your call** | **Not updated in
branch.** Existing `hover_actions_popover.test.tsx` still covers hover
behavior. You can **leave unchecked** and note “no test change; optional
follow-up to assert `focusTrapProps.preventScrollOnFocus`”, or add a
small test and then **check**. |
| Cloud / docker allowlist | **Yes** | No `kibana.yml` or plugin config
keys changed. |
| Breaking HTTP API | **Yes** | No public HTTP or plugin contract
changes. |
| Flaky Test Runner | **Yes** | No test files modified; FTR not
applicable. |
| Release notes + `release_note:*` label | **You + reviewer** | Include
the **Release note** line in the GitHub PR body; apply
**`release_note:fix`** (or whatever your team uses for bugfixes)—confirm
against
[guidelines](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/master/contributing.html#kibana-release-notes-process).
|
| Backport labels | **Reviewer / RM** | Don’t guess—Security / SDH
usually decides `backport:skip` vs target minors. Ask on PR if unsure. |
| Risks (RISK_MATRIX) | **Yes** | Low risk; see **Risk** section above.

body:
## Summary

The YOLO12 model page showed ✅ for inference/validation/training/export across detect, seg, pose, cls, and obb, but only detect `.pt` weights are published on `ultralytics/assets` — the other task variants are architecture-only (`.yaml` configs in `ultralytics/cfg/models/12/` that support training from scratch). This updates the supported tasks table and FAQ to reflect reality so users stop hitting `FileNotFoundError` when calling `YOLO("yolo12n-seg.pt")` and similar.

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
📝 This PR updates the YOLO12 docs to clearly show that official pretrained weights are currently available only for detection, while other YOLO12 task variants are config-only and must be trained from scratch.

### 📊 Key Changes
- ➕ Added a prominent warning in the YOLO12 documentation about **pretrained weights availability**.
- 📋 Expanded the task support table with a new **“Pretrained Weights”** column.
- ✅ Clarified that **YOLO12 detection** has official pretrained `.pt` weights available.
- ❌ Marked **YOLO12 segmentation, pose, classification, and OBB** as having **no official pretrained `.pt` weights** at this time.
- 🛠️ Explained that these non-detection variants are still supported via their `.yaml` model configs and can be **trained from scratch**.
- 🔁 Added guidance recommending **YOLO11** or **YOLO26** for users who need pretrained checkpoints for segmentation, pose, classification, or OBB.
- ✏️ Updated the FAQ/task-support text to reflect this limitation and avoid implying that all YOLO12 variants have ready-to-use pretrained models.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🎯 Prevents confusion for users who may expect downloadable pretrained YOLO12 weights for every task.
- 📚 Makes the documentation more accurate and transparent about what is officially released versus what is only architecturally supported.
- 🚀 Helps users choose the right model faster: use **YOLO12** for pretrained detection, or **YOLO11/YOLO26** when pretrained non-detection models are needed.
- 🧩 Sets clearer expectations for developers and researchers who want to use YOLO12 segmentation, pose, classification, or OBB—they will need to **train their own checkpoints first**.
- 💬 Reduces setup friction and support issues caused by missing weight files or incorrect assumptions about model availability.

## Summary

- Adds `autoFillEnumName?: boolean` to `PluginOptions`
- When enabled, the CLI plugin automatically adds `enumName` (derived from the TypeScript type name) to every detected enum property in DTOs

## Motivation

Issue #1815 — without `enumName`, every property that uses an enum type gets its own inline enum definition in the output spec, bloating the document and breaking code generators that expect named schemas. Setting `enumName` manually on every `@ApiProperty` is tedious. This option automates it at the plugin level.

- [ ] With `autoFillEnumName: true`, a DTO property typed as `StatusEnum` generates `{ enum: StatusEnum, enumName: "StatusEnum" }`

The `backend/.env` had an unresolved merge conflict that silently set `FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:3000` (Vite runs on 5173). Every API call from the frontend failed the CORS preflight — `err.response` was `undefined`, always hitting the generic fallback message.

// before

author: lorisleiva
body:
This PR adds a new `@solana/kit-plugin-signer` package that provides plugins for setting up the `payer` and `identity` signers on Kit clients. It introduces a consistent three-variant pattern where each plugin family offers a `signer*` variant (sets both payer and identity), a `payer*` variant (sets only payer), and an `identity*` variant (sets only identity).

The package includes five plugin families: `signer`/`payer`/`identity` for providing an existing signer, `generatedSigner`/`generatedPayer`/`generatedIdentity` for generating random keypairs, `generatedSignerWithSol`/`generatedPayerWithSol`/`generatedIdentityWithSol` for generating and funding keypairs, `signerFromFile`/`payerFromFile`/`identityFromFile` for loading keypairs from JSON files, and `airdropSigner`/`airdropPayer`/`airdropIdentity` for funding signers that are already installed on the client.

Some of these plugins are taken from the `@solana/kit-plugin-payer` package, which will be deprecated in a subsequent PR.

author: irongollem
body:
Closes the `v1/sections/` bullet on #142 and brings the Compendium edition in line with the rest of the app.

## What and why

The Reliquary Compendium was pulling from Open5e's **v2** `/v2/rulesets/` (2024 SRD / 5.5e) since it shipped — but every other Open5e endpoint we consume (spells / monsters / items / conditions / backgrounds / races) is on **v1** (2014 SRD 5.1). The Compendium was an island of 2024 rules in an otherwise-2014 app, with no campaign-level switch telling DMs which edition they were on.

Per the new tracking issue **#146** the right long-term move is a campaign-level ruleset switch (2014 ↔ 2024) with full v2 support across the app — but Open5e's v2 coverage is still patchy (no v2 backgrounds / conditions / feats / planes yet), so committing to 2024 today is premature. This PR brings the Compendium in line by switching the sync to v1 sections only.

When v2 coverage is complete enough that #146 can ship, the v2 fetch comes back as a version-aware path.

## Edge function changes

- Fetch from `https://api.open5e.com/v1/sections/` instead of `/v2/rulesets/`
- Tag rows `doc_slug: "srd-5.1"` (was `"srd-2024"`)
- Slug-prefix every section with `srd5_` to keep the namespace clean and avoid any future v2-vs-v1 collision
- Sections have free-text `parent` names in the v1 API; the function builds a `name → slug` lookup so children resolve to the right `parent_slug`
- **Cleanup**: every run starts with a `DELETE FROM srd_rules WHERE doc_slug IN ('srd-2024')` so previous v2 rows don't linger as orphans

Function response shape:
```json
{ "ok": true, "synced": 45, "deleted_stale": 317, "doc_slug": "srd-5.1", "sections_fetched": 45 }
```

## UI

**Zero changes to CompendiumTab.** With a single `doc_slug` in the table, the existing tree just shows v1 sections instead of v2 rulesets — no edition badge needed yet. That comes back when #146 lands and the table holds both editions side by side.

## Deploy

After merging:

```bash
supabase functions deploy sync-srd-rules
# then trigger it (Supabase dashboard → Edge Functions → Invoke, or curl)
```

The first run will delete the existing 317 v2 rule rows and replace them with the ~45 v1 section rows. **This is a destructive change to the Compendium contents** — DMs who relied on the 2024 rulings being there will see 2014 prose instead until v2 support lands. That's the intentional trade-off for cross-app consistency; #146 captures the path back.

## Test plan

- [x] Function compiles cleanly under deno's TS checker
- [x] `npm run build` — passes (no client changes touch the build)
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- [ ] Deploy + invoke — verify response payload includes `synced` count > 0 and `deleted_stale` matches the prior v2 row count
- [ ] Open `/rules` Compendium tab — verify v1 sections (Combat, Equipment, Magic, etc.) appear in the tree
- [ ] Verify no orphaned v2 rows in `srd_rules` (`select count(*) from srd_rules where doc_slug = 'srd-2024'` → 0)
- [ ] Search still works in the Compendium

Refs #142, #146

author: zena-park
body:
## Bug

A note (commitment) is bound to its sell-side token — the deposit that funds the trade. The previous reset effect bundled both tokens:

\`\`\`tsx
useEffect(() => {
  setSelectedCommitment(null);
  setManualPrice(\"\");
}, [sellTokenIdx, buyTokenIdx]);
\`\`\`

so every buy-token dropdown tweak wiped the user's note selection. Reported via "buy 토큰 셀렉트를 수정하면 기존에 커밋먼트 선택한게 해제된다."

## Fix

Split the effect:

- \`setSelectedCommitment(null)\` → only on \`sellTokenIdx\` change.
- \`setManualPrice(\"\")\` → still on either side, since the price ratio is tied to the (sell, buy) pair.

Safety net for the "buy-token change actually invalidates the note" case is already covered by the existing effect at \`page.tsx:337\` that clears the selection when \`selectedCommitment\` is no longer in \`availableNotes\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean
- [ ] Pick a commitment, change the BUY token → commitment stays selected
- [ ] Pick a commitment, change the SELL token → commitment clears (existing behavior preserved)
- [ ] Manual price field still clears on either side change

author: johnjezl
body:
## Summary

Two doc-only files covering the three capstone-critical x86-64 subsystems — preemptive multitasking, SMP, and GPU-accelerated model inference.

- **`docs/x86-64-capstone-gaps.md`** — state-of-the-art audit. Lists what works today (file:line citations), what's broken or untested, and a prioritized gap table. Preemption is functionally complete post-#91; remaining gaps are hardening (TSS IST, FXSAVE) and one medium-priority `sleep_ms()` bug that affects AP-pinned tasks. SMP boots 8/8 CPUs but lacks a reschedule IPI (up to 10 ms cross-CPU dispatch latency) and has work-stealing compiled but disabled. GPU: identification + VRAM R/W work; compute is blocked on GSP firmware which has never been booted (`0xBADF5040` on every engine register). x86-64 CPU inference is pure scalar because SSE is blocked by #72.
- **`docs/x86-64-capstone-gap-closure-plan.md`** — file-level, five-phase execution plan. Phases A–D (capstone scope, ~24 engineer-days) close every preemption + SMP gap and land inline-asm SSE inference. Phase E (post-capstone, ~52 days) is the full GSP-RM stack. Each workstream specifies deliverables at file:line granularity, design decisions with alternatives considered, regression tests by name, acceptance criteria, and ordering.

Reviewed against the current tree — every file, function, line reference, and configuration claim verified. Incorporates feedback from an independent code review (IPI handler calls `schedule()` not `scheduler_tick()` to avoid quantum double-ticking; `rq_lock` in `sched_try_steal` is the primary race defence not `preempt_disabled`; `sleep_ms()` TSC fix lifted from Phase D to Phase A so benchmarks don't get contaminated; FXSAVE/FXRSTOR added as its own workstream with multi-task-SSE as the explicit trigger).

## Test plan

- [x] No code changes — documentation only. No kernel, runtime, build, or test changes.
- [ ] Reviewer spot-check file:line citations match current tree (`git show HEAD:docs/x86-64-capstone-gaps.md`).
- [ ] Reviewer confirm the plan's phase ordering and dependency graph are implementable as described.

author: kduret
body:
## Summary

- Replace the deprecated/unmaintained `osixia/openldap` image with a lightweight [glauth](https://github.com/glauth/glauth)-based image (statically-linked Go binary, zero slapd/OpenLDAP dependency)
- Add `.github/docker/ldap/` with a multi-stage `Dockerfile` and a `config/config.cfg` declaring all users and groups
- Add `.github/workflows/docker-ldap.yml` to build and push the image to `ghcr.io/centreon/centreon/ldap`
- Rename the `openldap` docker-compose service to `ldap` and point it to the new image
- Update `README.md` accordingly

## Key design choices

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Server | glauth v2.4.0 — single Go binary, no OpenLDAP |
| `nameformat = "uid"` | Makes `(&(uid=*)(objectClass=posixAccount))` filterable |
| Admin bind DN | `cn=admin,dc=centreon,dc=com` kept via `name = "cn=admin"` workaround |
| `memberOf` | Computed automatically by glauth from group membership |
| Passwords | SHA-256 pre-hashed (password = username, admin = `centreon`) |

## Test plan

- [ ] Build the image locally: `docker build -t ldap .github/docker/ldap`
- [ ] Start with profile: `docker compose --profile ldap up`
- [ ] Verify bind: `ldapsearch -H ldap://localhost:389 -D "cn=admin,dc=centreon,dc=com" -w centreon -b "dc=centreon,dc=com" "(&(uid=*)(objectClass=posixAccount))"`
- [ ] Run LDAP e2e tests

author: nedunchezhiyan-m
body:
## Summary

- When two or more `@ApiXxxResponse` decorators on the same method share a status code, their `description` fields are now joined with `\n\n` instead of the later one silently overwriting the earlier
- `examples` objects from multiple same-status decorators are merged together
- All other fields (type, schema, headers) from the later decorator take precedence, preserving backward compatibility

## Motivation

Issue #2819 — applying `@ApiBadRequestResponse` twice to document different validation failure reasons was not possible; the second decorator silently replaced the first. Users had to concatenate descriptions manually or write custom wrapper decorators.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests pass: `npx vitest run`
- [ ] Three `@ApiBadRequestResponse` decorators on one method produce a single 400 response whose description contains all three descriptions separated by blank lines
- [ ] Two decorators with `examples` on the same status code produce merged examples

author: pinnocio
body:
### Motivation

- Remove the optional "consensus" synthesis pass and related UI to simplify the three-model compare workflow and reduce complexity in selection logic.
- Consolidate provider label strings into a single utility to avoid duplication and make labeling consistent across components.
- Fix a minor persisted-state initialization issue by avoiding a `useRef` clone pattern and using a stable initial value.

### Description

- Removed consensus-related state, UI blocks, and `generateConsensus` handlers from multiple client components (`DraftApp`, `LensSummarizer`, `PersonaCompiler`, `Summarizer`) so compare mode now shows direct model outputs only and lets users select one directly. 
- Deleted consensus endpoints on the server and removed imports for consensus handlers from `server/index.js`. 
- Extracted provider labels into a new module `utils/providerLabels.js` and updated `ModelComparison` and other components to import `providerLabel` from that new module instead of exporting it from `ModelComparison.jsx`. 
- Simplified `selectDirectResult` to only update `selectedResultKey` without trying to clear consensus, and removed several consensus-related helper variables (e.g. `consensusResult`, `selectedBaseProviderKey`, `canGenerateConsensus`).
- Simplified the `usePersistedState` hook by replacing the `useRef` clone with a `useState` memoized initial clone and updated `resetState` to use that stable initial value.

### Testing

- Ran the application build with `npm run build` and the build completed successfully. 
- Ran the test suite with `npm test` and all tests passed. 
- Verified the development server starts and the compare-mode UI renders the direct outputs and selection labels correctly in a local smoke test.

author: limars874
body: ## What does this PR do? `wecom` was the only active messaging platform missing from `PLATFORM_HINTS` in `agent/prompt_builder.py`. Without this entry, the AI model receives no system-level guidance that it can send files natively via `MEDIA:` syntax. As a result, when users ask the bot to send a file or image, it incorrectly responds that it lacks file-sending capability — even though `send_document`, `send_image_file`, and `send_voice` are fully implemented in `WeComAdapter`. This PR adds the missing `"wecom"` entry to `PLATFORM_HINTS`, consistent with all other supported platforms (`telegram`, `discord`, `slack`, `signal`, `whatsapp`, etc.). ## Related Issue N/A ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `agent/prompt_builder.py`: Added `"wecom"` entry to `PLATFORM_HINTS` dict, instructing the model to use `MEDIA:/path` syntax for native file delivery on WeCom (企业微信). Covers images (≤10 MB), documents (≤20 MB), videos, and AMR voice messages. ## How to Test 1. Configure a WeCom AI Bot and connect Hermes via `hermes gateway` 2. In a WeCom DM with the bot, ask it to generate and send a file, e.g. *"写一个简单的 markdown 文档发给我"* 3. **Before this fix:** the bot responds that it has no file-sending capability 4. **After this fix:** the bot creates the file and includes `MEDIA:/path/to/file.md` in its response, which the gateway intercepts and delivers as a native WeCom attachment Tested end-to-end on a live WeCom AI Bot deployment. The bot successfully generated and delivered a `.xlsx` file as a native WeCom document attachment after this change. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [ ] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: debian 12 server ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

author: werner291
body:
Hi, I'm Werner. I've got an interest in bioinformatics, especially in cancer genomics, so I figured I'd try to find some connections to the domain through some open-source contributions. I saw your issue #10 and figured I'd send in a PR.

Closes #10.

## What this does

- Replaces the manual JSON formatting in `write_json` with serde (Rust's standard serialization library). The field names and numeric values are unchanged — a unit test parses both the old and new output as JSON and compares them field by field.
- Adds a `--sample-name` (`-s`) flag. When provided, a `SAMPLE_NAME` field is included in the JSON output. When omitted, the field is absent, so existing scripts that parse the JSON are unaffected.

## Things we noticed along the way

- **NaN in JSON output:** When no reads are processed, `FRACTION_DUPLICATION` is 0/0 which the old code wrote as `NaN` — but `NaN` is not valid JSON and will break strict parsers. This PR emits `null` instead. Happy to split it out if you'd prefer a separate fix.
- **Test coverage:** We couldn't verify end-to-end behavior because there are no integration tests with BAM fixtures. The unit tests confirm the JSON values match, but we had no way to run the full pipeline and diff the output. If it would be useful, I'd be happy to help set up a small integration test with a sample BAM file.

## Sample output

Without `--sample-name`:
```json
{"UNPAIRED_READS_EXAMINED":1000,"PAIRED_READS_EXAMINED":5000,...}
```

With `--sample-name my_sample`:
```json
{"SAMPLE_NAME":"my_sample","UNPAIRED_READS_EXAMINED":1000,...}
```

- Update `generate_widget_example_json.py` to remove `data: {}` from the built-in few-shot JSON examples and to stop emitting `data` when parsing or serializing parsed tool calls. 
- Update `generate_genui_tsx.py` to stop creating/expecting `data` fields in `parse_tool_calls`, `build_prompt`, `check_tool_calls_used`, and related logic, and to change prompt text to instruct usage of `params` only.

author: copilot
body:
The README was the default `create-next-app` boilerplate — no mention of what the project does, how to run it, or how the pieces fit together.

## Changes

- **Overview & features** — project purpose, key capabilities (donor registration, hospital network, blood requests, inventory, donation logs, live stats dashboard)
- **Tech stack table** — frontend (Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4) and backend (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy async, Pydantic v2, PostgreSQL)

## Summary
Queue workers currently perform a single execution lookup before failing. In queue mode, that lookup can intermittently miss even though the execution becomes available a short moment later.

author: lucasbergman94
body:
## Contexto

O fix anterior (PR #5) usando regex em \`pet_owners.cell_phone\` + \`Op.notIn\` + \`Sequelize.literal\` não estava emitindo o NOT IN corretamente em produção — test personas continuavam em Geral apesar do deploy. Query SQL isolada funcionava, mas via Sequelize + findAndCountAll + distinct + includes complexos a subquery não aplicava.

## Causa raiz

\`Op.notIn\` + \`Sequelize.literal\` de subquery complexa não é emitido dentro do mesmo WHERE que o Sequelize usa pra paginar contatos com includes \`separate:true\`. O mesmo repository já tem um [comentário explicativo](src/api/repositories/chat-history.repository.js#L36-L39) sobre \`required: true\` quebrar em combinação com \`separate: true\` — solução adotada sempre foi subquery SQL raw via \`Op.in\` + condição AND separada.

## Fix

Troca pra o marcador **\`chat_history.path LIKE 'test-persona|%'\`**, que é gravado automaticamente pela EF \`chat-history-logger\` ([index.ts:73-79](../supabase/functions/chat-history-logger/index.ts)) pra chats vindos de \`5500000000XXX\`. Essa é a mesma source of truth usada pelo skill \`/delete-test-personas\`.

### Mudanças

- Novo helper \`buildTestChatFilter\` retorna \`{ op: 'in' | 'notIn' }\` + constante \`TEST_CONTACT_IDS_SUBQUERY\`
- Aplicado como condição AND separada em \`additionalConditions\` nas 3 rotas: \`getAllContactsWithMessages\`, \`getAllContactsBeingAttended\`, \`getAllContactsMessagesWithNoFilters\`
- Pattern \`Op.in/notIn\` + \`Sequelize.literal\` de subquery, mesmo pattern que já funciona com \`filters.tags\`
- \`getTestContactsCount\` refeito com LEFT JOIN em \`pet_owner_clinics\` (pega test personas sem clinic association — 1/31 no banco atual)
- Removidos \`buildTestPhoneFilter\` e \`TEST_PHONE_REGEX\` (substituídos)

## Vantagens vs. abordagem anterior

| Aspecto | Antes (cell_phone regex) | Depois (path prefix) |
|---|---|---|
| Source of truth | Heurística no telefone | Marcador explícito gravado pela EF |
| JOIN com pet_owners | Obrigatório | Opcional |
| Contatos sem pet_owner | Falso positivo | Tratados corretamente |
| Consistência com \`/delete-test-personas\` | Diferente | Idêntica |
| Sequelize quirks | \`Op.notIn\` não emite | \`Op.in\` + condição AND funciona |

## Test plan

- [ ] Rotas autenticadas retornam 401 após deploy
- [ ] Aba Geral em debugger NÃO lista Persona P##
- [ ] Aba Testes lista as 30 personas com chat e clinic
- [ ] Filtros de tags/responsibility/unread continuam funcionando
- [ ] \`/delete-test-personas\` continua limpando tudo normalmente

## PRs relacionados

- Docs: \`Matheus3FY/Latta#TBD\` (adiciona \`docs/knowledge/test-personas.md\` consolidando os marcadores)
- Frontend: \`Latta-app/frontend#TBD\` (troca cor da aba Testes pro gradiente de Geral/Suporte)

author: genspark-ai-developer[bot]
body:
## Problème

Les pages et hooks admin effectuaient des lectures et mutations directement via `createClient()` (clé anon) côté navigateur. La protection des données PII (emails, téléphones, siret, décisions de modération, badges de confiance) reposait **uniquement sur la RLS Supabase**. Si la RLS a une faille, l'impact est élevé.

## Correctif

Chaque opération sensible passe désormais par une route API Next.js qui :
- vérifie la session et le rôle admin/modérateur via `getAdminUser()`
- utilise `createAdminClient()` (service role) pour les mutations contrôlées
- valide toutes les entrées avec Zod (allowlist strict)

## Nouvelles routes API serveur

| Route | Méthode | Remplace |
|-------|---------|----------|
| `/api/admin/users` | GET | `supabase.from('profiles').select('*')` côté client |
| `/api/admin/confiance` | GET | Requêtes directes sur `reviews`, `trust_profile_stats`, `profiles` |
| `/api/admin/confiance/[id]` | PATCH | `supabase.from('reviews').update()` + `profile_badges.upsert()` |
| `/api/admin/artisans/[id]` | GET/PATCH | Validation/rejet des dossiers artisans |
| `/api/admin/contenu/[table]/[id]` | PATCH/DELETE | Mutations sur listings, forum_posts, equipment_items, reviews |
| `/api/admin/moderation/[id]/decision` | PATCH | `moderation_queue.update()` + propagation source table |
| `/api/admin/moderation/[id]/trust` | PATCH | `profiles.update({ trust_level })` |

## Sécurité renforcée sur chaque route

- **`getAdminUser()`** : vérifie JWT + profil + rôle admin/moderator côté serveur
- **`createAdminClient()`** : service role key — bypass RLS contrôlé (jamais exposé au client)
- **Zod** : validation stricte des inputs (allowlist des tables, enums, longueurs max)
- L'auteur des mutations est toujours récupéré côté serveur (`actor.id`) — le client ne peut pas se substituer

## Pages/hooks mis à jour

- `admin/utilisateurs/page.tsx` → `fetchUsers()` → GET `/api/admin/users`
- `admin/confiance/page.tsx` → `load()` → GET `/api/admin/confiance`, mutations → PATCH `/api/admin/confiance/[id]`
- `admin/moderation/[id]/_hooks/useModerationDetail.ts` → `handleDecision` + `handleTrustChange` → routes API
- `admin/contenu/_hooks/use{Listings,ForumPosts,Equipment,Reviews}.ts` → `deleteItem`/`toggle*` → PATCH|DELETE `/api/admin/contenu/…`

## Tests

- **676/676 ✅** (dont le test de sécurité `no-debug-routes` qui vérifie la présence d'auth sur chaque route)
- **TypeScript : 0 erreur ✅**

author: copilot
body:
Bootstraps this repo as a PyTorch library for training and evaluating Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) where concept representations are continuous (real-valued) rather than binary.

## Package: `cbm/`

- **`models.py`** – `ConceptEncoder → TaskPredictor` bottleneck architecture; `ConceptBottleneckModel` supports `joint`, `sequential`, and `independent` training modes; test-time concept intervention via `intervention` / `intervention_mask`
- **`datasets.py`** – `SyntheticContinuousDataset`: generates `x → c (linear projection + noise) → y` triples; `SyntheticContinuousDataset.splits()` for train/val/test
- **`training.py`** – `train_epoch` / `evaluate_epoch` per-step primitives; `train()` high-level loop with early stopping; sequential mode auto-runs two phases (encoder-only → predictor-only)
- **`evaluate.py`** – `concept_mae`, `concept_r2`, `task_accuracy`, `task_r2`, `full_evaluation`, `intervention_gain` (measures task lift from ground-truth concept injection)
- **`utils.py`** – `set_seed`, checkpoint save/load, `plot_training_curves`

## Experiment script

`experiments/train_cbm.py` – end-to-end CLI covering all training modes and tasks.

## Quick start

```python
from cbm import ConceptBottleneckModel, SyntheticContinuousDataset
from cbm.datasets import make_dataloaders
from cbm.training import train
from cbm.evaluate import full_evaluation, intervention_gain

train_ds, val_ds, test_ds = SyntheticContinuousDataset.splits(
    n_samples=2000, in_features=20, n_concepts=5, task="classification"
)
model = ConceptBottleneckModel(in_features=20, n_concepts=5, n_outputs=1, mode="joint")
train(model, *make_dataloaders(train_ds, val_ds, test_ds), alpha=0.5, n_epochs=100)

print(full_evaluation(model, test_loader))
# {'concept_mae': 0.24, 'concept_r2': 0.91, 'task_accuracy': 0.88}

print(intervention_gain(model, test_loader))
# {'baseline': 0.88, 'intervened': 0.94}
```

Loss: `α · MSE(ĉ, c) + (1−α) · task_loss` — `α` controls the concept supervision strength. Concept encoder output is unconstrained by default; optionally bounded via `sigmoid`/`tanh`.
