author: freemans13
body:
## Summary

During a reorg reset, invalid moveBack blocks are handled by BlockValidation's background job (`setTxMinedStatus(unsetMined=true)`), which sets `unmined_since` on their transactions. Previously, `reset()` called `loadUnminedTransactions` without waiting for this background processing to complete, so those txs still had `unmined_since=NULL` and were invisible to the unmined iterator.

**Changes:**
- Add `waitForBlockMinedSet` — polls until BlockValidation has finished processing each invalid moveBack block (exponential backoff, context-cancellable)
- Call it for each invalid moveBack block before `loadUnminedTransactions` runs
- On context cancellation: return error. On retries exhausted: proceed with warning (txs may be recovered on subsequent resets)
- Short-circuit on non-retriable errors (ErrBlockNotFound)

- [x] `make lint` — 0 issues

…F fixes

Security fixes:
1. CRITICAL: Replace access token in URL params with one-time auth code exchange
   - Access tokens were exposed in browser URL bar, history, server logs, Referer headers
   - Now uses a 256-bit random code stored in Redis (2-min TTL) exchanged via POST

2. CRITICAL: Fix OAuth state verification on Vercel Serverless
   - Session-based state failed because serverless functions are stateless
   - Now stores OAuth state in Redis directly (not express-session)
   - State is verified against Redis before passport authentication
   - State is one-time use (deleted after verification) to prevent replay attacks

3. MEDIUM: Add /auth/exchange-code to CSRF exempt paths
   - The one-time code serves as its own CSRF protection

author: vivswan
body:
## Summary

- Fix VS Code internal `modelOptions` keys (e.g. `_capturingTokenCorrelationId`) leaking to LiteLLM backends and causing 400 errors
- Fix `bump-version` script printing the same version on both sides of the arrow
- Replace `provider.real.test.ts` with a new host-fidelity test layer that exercises the extension through the real VS Code LM API (`vscode.lm.selectChatModels` / `model.sendRequest`) instead of calling provider methods directly

## Changes

### Bug fixes

**Filter VS Code internal keys from modelOptions** (`src/provider.ts`)
- Skip any `modelOptions` key starting with `_` before forwarding to LiteLLM
- VS Code injects private fields like `_capturingTokenCorrelationId` into `modelOptions` at runtime; forwarding them caused Azure/OpenAI-compatible backends to reject requests with "Unknown parameter" 400 errors

**Fix bump-version script** (`scripts/bump-version.js`)
- Capture `currentVersion` before overwriting `packageJson.version`, so the log and stdout output show `0.1.0 -> 0.2.0` instead of `0.2.0 -> 0.2.0`

### Test infrastructure overhaul

**New host-fidelity test layer** (`src/test/host-fidelity.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-server.js`)

The previous `provider.real.test.ts` called `provideLanguageModelChatResponse()` directly, bypassing the VS Code LM host layer entirely. This missed host-injected fields, frozen/readonly objects, real `LanguageModelChatMessage` conversion, and streaming via `response.stream`.

The new suite enters the provider through the real VS Code LM API and operates in two modes:

**Capture mode** (37 tests, deterministic) — backed by a programmable local HTTP server:
- Model discovery: vendor, family, token limits, `countTokens` via host API
- Request contract: underscore-key filtering, provider-owned field protection, `modelOptions` pass-through (`response_format`, `reasoning_effort`, `top_k`), `stream_options`, message role conversion, multi-turn conversation ordering
- Multimodal: image→`image_url` blocks, multiple images, text/image ordering, PDF→`file` blocks, JSON data part→inline text
- Tool round-trip: tool call + tool result serialization, mixed text + tool calls, tool definitions with schema/enum, multiple tools
- Response contract: plain text, structured `delta.content` arrays, reasoning (`reasoning_content`, `reasoning` field variants), structured Anthropic thinking objects, text-then-tool-call, parallel tool calls, usage-only final chunks, cache token trailers, cancellation, HTTP 400/401 errors

**Live mode** (17 tests, against real LiteLLM) — replaces the old `real-test` runner:
- Model discovery, raw HTTP endpoint probes
- Streaming chat: simple, multi-turn, substantial output, internal key filtering, cancellation
- Tool calling: auto-mode (accepts both tool call and text), multiple tools

**Test-only instrumentation** (`src/extension.ts`)
- `litellm._test.setSecrets` — configure provider secrets programmatically
- `litellm._test.refreshModels` — force model re-fetch to avoid stale model lists
- Both guarded behind `context.extensionMode !== ExtensionMode.Production`

**Removed**
- `src/test/provider.real.test.ts` — all tests consolidated into `provider.test.ts` (unit) or `host-fidelity.test.ts`
- `scripts/real-test.js` — replaced by `scripts/host-fidelity-test.js`

**Config changes**

author: fw-bot
body:
Point of Sale users only have read access on pos.payment.method. When the stored Viva.com bearer token expires or the API returns invalid credentials, _bearer_token() fetches a new token .
That write ran as the POS user and raised an AccessError, although the user was only paying—not editing configuration.

Steps to reproduce:
-------------------
* Configure  Viva.com as payment method.
* Open the POS as a user with only Point of Sale / User (not Administrator).
* Pay with Viva until the OAuth token must be refreshed (e.g. after expiry or after Viva rejects the current token).

> Observation:
 AccessError: You are not allowed to modify 'Point of Sale Payment Methods' (pos.payment.method) records.

Why the fix:
------------
Persist the refreshed viva_com_bearer_token with sudo().write() so the ORM does not require write ACL on pos.payment.method for that internal side effect of an already authorized Viva RPC.

### Motivation
- Introduce governance and deterministic matching for account/fund alias collisions to avoid ambiguous imports and enable steward resolution workflows.
- Enforce normalization and active-row uniqueness hygiene for `account`, `fund`, and their alias tables to reduce data drift and accidental duplicates.
- Provide migration, rollback, validation and risk documentation to support safe cutover and remediation.

- Add forward migration `scripts/sql/master_data_harmonization_forward.sql` that creates the `alias_review_queue` table, adds constraints, and creates normalized unique/validation indexes for `account`, `fund`, `account_alias`, and `fund_alias`, and initially populates the queue for active alias collisions.  Corresponding rollback and validation SQL files were added as `master_data_harmonization_rollback.sql` and `master_data_harmonization_validation.sql`.

body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** Unsafe configuration of `DocumentBuilderFactory` and `SAXParserFactory` in `ReaderUtils` (both `platform` and `catalog` modules) allowed parsing of external entities and DTDs.
🎯 **Impact:** Vulnerability to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, which can lead to sensitive file disclosure, server-side request forgery (SSRF), and denial of service (DoS) when parsing untrusted XML input.
🔧 **Fix:** Explicitly disabled DOCTYPE declarations (`disallow-doctype-decl`) and external entities (`external-general-entities`, `external-parameter-entities`, `load-external-dtd`). Configuration exceptions are caught, logged securely, and throw a `RuntimeException` to fail fast and securely.
✅ **Verification:** Ran test suite to verify no regressions were introduced. Spotless formatting was applied to modified modules. Recorded the vulnerability pattern and mitigation strategy in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

body:
Closed https://github.com/Shopify/cli/issues/7275

### WHY are these changes introduced?

When E2E tests fail, some assertions already had error context (e.g., `build failed:\nstderr: ...`) but others didn't, the error message only shows "Expected: 0, Received: 1" without the CLI output that caused the failure. This makes it hard to diagnose issues, especially in CI where you can't re-run interactively.

### WHAT is this pull request doing?

Adds error context (stdout/stderr) to all `expect(exitCode).toBe(0)` assertions that were missing it.

Before:
```typescript
expect(initResult.exitCode).toBe(0)
```

After:
```typescript
expect(initResult.exitCode, `create-app failed:\nstdout: ${initResult.stdout}\nstderr: ${initResult.stderr}`).toBe(0)
```

**Files changed:** 6 test files — `app-dev-server`, `app-scaffold`, `commands`, `smoke`, `smoke-pty`

### How to test your changes?

author: copilot
body:
Two bugs prevented the reboot flow from working: on the local machine, `await apiFetch("/api/reboot")` hangs forever (server dies before responding), so the overlay and reconnect poll never start. On LAN, `waitForServerReboot` aborted each probe after 5 s — shorter than mDNS re-registration time — so the spinner never resolved.

## `constants.js`
- Added `REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 12000` (probe AbortController — mDNS needs headroom)
- Added `REBOOT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 4000` (fire-and-forget reboot POST)
- Added `REBOOT_INITIAL_DELAY = 25000` (NixOS shutdown takes 20-40 s)

## `update.js` — `doReboot()`
Replaced `apiFetch` (which awaits `res.json()` and hangs when the server dies) with plain `fetch` + `AbortController`:
```js
var rebootCtrl = new AbortController();
setTimeout(function() { rebootCtrl.abort(); }, REBOOT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT);
fetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST", signal: rebootCtrl.signal }).catch(function() {});
setTimeout(waitForServerReboot, REBOOT_INITIAL_DELAY);
```

## `update.js` — `waitForServerReboot()`
- AbortController timeout: `REBOOT_CHECK_INTERVAL` (5 s) → `REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT` (12 s)
- Added `headers: { "Connection": "close" }` to avoid reusing stale keepalive connections
- Failsafe reload threshold: 30 s → 90 s

## `security.js` — security-reset reboot handler
Removed `async`/`await apiFetch(...)` entirely. Overlay display and `waitForServerReboot` now execute synchronously before the fire-and-forget fetch, so the reconnect flow always starts regardless of whether the server responds:
```js
rebootBtn.addEventListener("click", function() {
  rebootBtn.disabled = true;
  rebootBtn.textContent = "Rebooting…";
  if ($rebootOverlay) $rebootOverlay.classList.add("visible");
  setTimeout(waitForServerReboot, REBOOT_INITIAL_DELAY);
  var rebootCtrl = new AbortController();
  setTimeout(function() { rebootCtrl.abort(); }, REBOOT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT);
  fetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST", signal: rebootCtrl.signal }).catch(function() {});
}, { once: true });
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Two related reboot bugs need to be fixed

### Bug 1 — Reboot button does nothing on the local computer after system update

**File:** `app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/update.js` (line 177) and `app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/security.js` (lines 160-168)

**Root cause:** The `doReboot()` function on line 177 of `update.js` calls:
```js
apiFetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST" }).catch(function() {});
```

`apiFetch()` (defined in `helpers.js` lines 52-60) does `await fetch(...)` then `await res.json()`. When the user clicks reboot **on the local machine itself**, the web server process is killed by the reboot before it can send a response. The `fetch()` promise hangs forever — it never resolves and never rejects (no network error because it's localhost, the connection just dies). The `.catch()` never fires. **But that's not the main problem** — the real issue is that `setTimeout(waitForServerReboot, 15000)` on line 179 DOES still fire.

**The critical bug is in `security.js` lines 160-168:**
```js
rebootBtn.addEventListener("click", async function() {
  rebootBtn.disabled = true;
  rebootBtn.textContent = "Rebooting…";
  try {
    await apiFetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST" });  // ← HANGS FOREVER on local machine
  } catch (_) {}
  if ($rebootOverlay) $rebootOverlay.classList.add("visible");  // ← NEVER REACHED
  setTimeout(waitForServerReboot, REBOOT_CHECK_INTERVAL);       // ← NEVER REACHED
}, { once: true });
```

Because `await apiFetch(...)` hangs, the reboot overlay is never shown and `waitForServerReboot` is never started. The button just says "Rebooting…" and nothing else ever happens. The machine reboots but the user never sees feedback.

**Fix needed for both files:**
1. In `update.js` `doReboot()`: Replace `apiFetch` with plain `fetch` wrapped in an `AbortController` with a 4-second timeout. We don't need the JSON response from a fire-and-forget reboot call.
2. In `security.js` security reset reboot handler: Same fix — use plain `fetch` with `AbortController` timeout. **Critically**, move the reboot overlay display and `waitForServerReboot` call to execute BEFORE the fetch, or at minimum don't use `await` so they always execute.

### Bug 2 — Reboot modal stuck spinning on LAN (never detects reboot completed)

**File:** `app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/update.js` (lines 182-208) and `app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/constants.js` (line 8)

**Root cause:** `waitForServerReboot()` creates an `AbortController` that aborts each health-check fetch after `REBOOT_CHECK_INTERVAL` (5000ms = 5 seconds). On LAN, the user accesses the hub via `sovransystemsos.local` (mDNS) or a LAN IP. After reboot:
- mDNS name re-registration takes 10-30 seconds
- The browser's DNS resolution for the hostname may be cached as "failed"
- Each fetch probe gets aborted after just 5 seconds, before DNS can resolve
- The server IS back, but the probe never successfully connects
- Result: the reboot overlay spins forever

**Fixes needed:**

1. In `constants.js`, add a new constant for the reboot probe timeout (separate from REBOOT_CHECK_INTERVAL):
```js
const REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 12000;  // 12 seconds — mDNS re-registration is slow
```

2. In `update.js` `doReboot()`: Increase the initial delay before first probe from 15000ms to 25000ms. NixOS shutdown after a system update takes 20-40 seconds.

3. In `update.js` `waitForServerReboot()`: 
   - Use `REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT` (12s) for the AbortController timeout instead of `REBOOT_CHECK_INTERVAL` (5s)
   - Add `headers: { "Connection": "close" }` to the fetch to prevent stale keepalive connections
   - Increase the failsafe timer from 30000ms to 90000ms (NixOS full reboot after update can take over 60s total)

### Summary of all changes needed:

**`app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/constants.js`:**
- Add `const REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 12000;`

**`app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/update.js`:**
- `doReboot()`: Replace `apiFetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST" })` with a plain `fetch` wrapped in an AbortController (4s timeout). Change initial delay from 15000 to 25000.
- `waitForServerReboot()`: Use REBOOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT (12s) for the AbortController timeout. Add `Connection: close` header. Change failsafe from 30000 to 90000.

**`app/sovran_systemsos_web/static/js/security.js`:**
- Security reset reboot handler (lines 160-168): Replace `await apiFetch("/api/reboot", { method: "POST" })` with a fire-and-forget plain `fetch` with AbortController timeout. Show the reboot overlay and call `waitForServerReboot` BEFORE or independently of the fetch — do NOT await the fetch.

author: masamoto1982
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the hedged race execution system to pass original code-block tokens directly to race functions instead of pre-compiled `ExecutableCode`. This enables proper reconstruction of the plain execution path and improves validation logic for epoch checking.

## Key Changes

- **Token-based plain path reconstruction**: Modified `execute_hedged_map_kernel`, `execute_hedged_predicate_kernel`, and `execute_hedged_fold_kernel` to accept `Option<&[Token]>` instead of `&ExecutableCode`. When tokens are available (code blocks), they're reconstructed as `ExecutableCode::CodeBlock` for the plain path; when unavailable (word names), the race is skipped entirely.

- **Epoch validation refinement**: Changed epoch comparison from comparing full `EpochSnapshot` to only comparing `dictionary_epoch` and `module_epoch`, excluding `execution_epoch` which changes during normal execution. Updated `validate_winner` and `validate_hedged_winner` signatures to accept `EpochSnapshot` references.

- **Improved error handling in races**: When the plain path fails but the quantized path succeeds, the quantized result is now accepted (with appropriate metrics and tracing) rather than propagating the plain error. This reflects that quantized execution is the primary path.

- **Purity-based hedging policy**: Enhanced `can_hedge_word` to use the purity table, implementing an allowlist policy where only words explicitly marked as `Pure` can be hedged. Unknown words are conservatively rejected.

- **Metrics cleanup**: Removed redundant `hedged_race_cancel_count` increments that were paired with `hedged_race_winner_quantized_count`.

- **Updated all HOF operations**: Applied token extraction and passing to `op_map`, `op_filter`, `op_any`, `op_all`, `op_count`, `op_fold`, and `op_scan`.

## Implementation Details

- Token extraction happens early in each operation via `code_val.as_code_block().map(|t| t.to_vec())` before executable code extraction
- The `None` case for `plain_tokens` (e.g., word-name kernels) short-circuits to quantized execution, avoiding unnecessary race setup
- Epoch snapshots are now captured at spawn time and stored in `HedgedCandidateResult` for later validation
- Trace messages now include `reason=plain-error` when quantized wins due to plain path failure

body:
## What

Converts subagent system from blocking (synchronous) to async (fire-and-forget with polling).

### Before
- `subagent_spawn` blocks the calling agent's turn until the sub-agent finishes (120s timeout)
- No way to check progress mid-flight
- Calling agent burns context window waiting on nothing

### After
- `subagent_spawn` returns immediately with session ID
- New `subagent_status` tool — check elapsed time, iterations, tools used, partial/final response
- No default timeout — agents run until done or killed
- `subagent_send` is also async — fire and poll

### Tools changed
| Tool | Change |
|------|--------|
| `subagent_spawn` | Removed `mode` param, always async, returns immediately |
| `subagent_status` | **New** — poll progress/results |
| `subagent_send` | Now async — returns immediately |
| `subagent_list` | No change |
| `subagent_kill` | No change |

### Files
- `src/tools/subagent.ts` — tool definitions + handlers
- `src/agents/subagent-manager.ts` — async session lifecycle

Fixes delegation timeouts that blocked families.app Phase 2 work.

author: knottnt
body:
Issue #, if available:

Description of changes:
This PR adds support for nested union types to the code-generator. Prior to this change if a `union` shape contained a member that was itself a `union` the code-generator would produce non-compiling code in two ways:

1. When setting the values from the API response the generated code would not use a type switch for the nested union member and attempt directly access fields as if they were a `structure`.
2. When setting the SDK payload the generated code would attempt to dereference the union member.

To address this this PR applies two fixes.
1. In `setResourceForUnion` check if the member is a union and force `Shape.Type` to `union` before recursing
2. In `setSDKForUnion` prevent dereference of member value if member is a union itself.

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request introduces performance optimizations for paginating high-volume organization audit logs by enabling advanced cursor-based pagination.

**Key Changes:**
* **Optimized Cursor Paginator:** Introduces a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` designed for high-traffic endpoints. This paginator supports negative offsets, allowing for more efficient bidirectional and reverse pagination across large datasets without requiring full dataset scans.
* **Conditional Audit Log Optimization:** Updates the Organization Audit Logs API endpoint to utilize the new optimized paginator. This feature is conditionally activated only when the `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter is provided **and** the requesting user has elevated permissions (either a superuser or a member with global access). Standard users or requests without the parameter will continue to use the default `DateTimePaginator`.
* **Enhanced Offset Handling:** Modifies the base pagination logic to safely process negative offsets when navigating backwards (`cursor.is_prev`), ensuring boundary conditions are handled correctly by the underlying queryset.

author: eboody
body:
## Summary

- reorganize `statum-macros` into clearer internal subsystems
- move source-observation helpers under `statum-macros/src/source/`
- split `state`, machine emission, and transition resolution into focused modules
- add shared semantic contracts and an internal architecture note
- restore the canonical primary-branch invariant for transition return types
- add regression coverage for invalid primary-branch transition wrappers

## Details

This keeps the public macro surface the same while making `statum-macros` easier to navigate as three internal layers:

1. source observation
2. semantic resolution
3. emission and diagnostics

The structural changes in this PR are:

- `statum-macros/src/source/` now owns file analysis, module-path lookup, and source-backed candidate queries
- `statum-macros/src/state/` now owns `#[state]` parsing, validation, registry storage, and emission
- `statum-macros/src/machine/emission/` is split into support scaffolding, builders, and presentation/introspection output
- `statum-macros/src/transition/resolve/` is split into alias expansion, shape parsing, and strict-vs-relaxed strategy code
- `statum-macros/src/validators/` now has explicit contract and planning modules
- `statum-macros/src/contracts.rs` provides shared internal handoff types
- `statum-macros/ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the intended subsystem boundaries

This PR also fixes a transition-validation regression: wrapper return shapes now have to resolve to the target machine in the primary branch, instead of passing just because a later branch mentions the machine. That restores the documented canonical contract and closes the matching strict `#[introspect(return = ...)]` hole.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Notes

- The public API stays the same.
- Strict introspection stays the authoritative fail-closed path.
- Relaxed behavior stays source-backed.
- Added regression coverage for invalid `Result<Error, Machine<Next>>`-style primary-branch shapes in both strict and non-strict modes.

author: hardwarebob
body:
## Task #254: ozma-agent-ui: cross-platform CI build matrix + artifact upload

Add GitHub Actions CI for `ozma-agent-ui` on all three target platforms.

**File: `.github/workflows/agent-ui.yml`**

```yaml
name: ozma-agent-ui

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'ozma-agent-ui/**'
      - 'ozma-agent/src/approvals.rs'
      - 'ozma-agent/src/api.rs'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-ui.yml'
  pull_request:
    paths: ['ozma-agent-ui/**']

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-22.04
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            artifact: ozma-agent-ui-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
          - os: windows-2022
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            artifact: ozma-agent-ui-windows-x86_64.zip
          - os: macos-14           # Apple Silicon runner
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            artifact: ozma-agent-ui-macos-aarch64.tar.gz

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-agent-ui-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}

      - name: Install Linux deps
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo apt-get install -y libdbus-1-dev libssl-dev pkg-config

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p ozma-agent-ui

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p ozma-agent-ui
        # Note: tray tests require display; headless tests only
        env:
          RUST_TEST_THREADS: 1

      - name: Package (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist/ozma-agent-ui
          cp target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/ozma-agent-ui dist/ozma-agent-ui/
          tar -czf ${{ matrix.artifact }} -C dist ozma-agent-ui/

      - name: Package (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path dist/ozma-agent-ui
          Copy-Item target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/ozma-agent-ui.exe dist/ozma-agent-ui/
          Compress-Archive -Path dist/ozma-agent-ui/* -DestinationPath ${{ matrix.artifact }}

      - name: Package (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist/ozma-agent-ui
          cp target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/ozma-agent-ui dist/ozma-agent-ui/
          tar -czf ${{ matrix.artifact }} -C dist ozma-agent-ui/

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          retention-days: 7
```

**Headless test compatibility:**
- Any test that creates a tray icon or opens an egui window must be `#[cfg(not(ci))]` or use a `--headless` test feature
- Add `[features] headless = []` to `ozma-agent-ui/Cargo.toml`
- In tests that require display: `#[cfg(not(feature = "headless"))]`
- CI passes `--features headless` to skip display-dependent tests

**Update existing CI** (`.github/workflows/rust.yml` or equivalent):
- Add `ozma-agent-ui` to the workspace test matrix
- Ensure the Linux job installs `libdbus-1-dev`

**Acceptance:**
- All three matrix legs pass `cargo build` on their respective runners
- `cargo test -p ozma-agent-ui --features headless` passes on all three
- Artifacts uploaded for each platform on every push to main
- CI runtime under 10 minutes per leg (use cache)

**Spec:** `internal/specs/build-site-agent-ui.md` → Tier 4

## Result

Cost estimates may be inaccurate when using streaming and caching.

author: copilot
body:
Five independent bugs in the quiz/dashboard/stats flow, ranging from a threshold miscalibration causing mastery to always show "ej påbörjad", to stats mixing data across subjects.

## Changes

### Category mastery always "ej påbörjad" (`stores/progress.js`)
`categoryMastery` required `bucket >= REVIEWING (3)`, which needs 2 correct answers across 2 separate sessions. Changed to count `totalSeen > 0` — any answered question counts as progress.

### "Totalt rätt" = unique correct % (`DailyStats.vue`, `DashboardView.vue`)
Was showing overall answer accuracy (`correct / seen`). Now shows the fraction of available subject questions answered correctly at least once (`totalCorrect >= 1`). `DailyStats` accepts a `questions` prop; dashboard passes `subjectQuestions`.

```js
// Before: accuracy of all answers across all subjects
const totalAccuracy = Math.round(total.value.accuracy * 100)

// After: % of this subject's questions ever answered correctly
const correct = props.questions.filter(q => (progress.progress[q.id]?.totalCorrect || 0) > 0).length
Math.round(correct / props.questions.length * 100)
```

### Scroll to explanation after answering (`QuizView.vue`)
After `answerQuestion`, scrolls `explanationRef` into view via `nextTick`.

### Post-answer option preview (`QuizView.vue`, `OptionButton.vue`)
Removed `:disabled="answered"` from `OptionButton`. `QuizView` now tracks a reactive `previewedIndices` Set. Pressing A/B/C/D (or clicking) after answering toggles inline feedback for that option with an indigo highlight. Cleared on next question.

### Per-subject stats overview (`StatsView.vue`)
"Totalt svar" and "Träffsäkerhet" overview cards used `progress.totalStats` (all subjects combined). Added `subjectStats` computed that filters progress entries to the selected subject's question IDs.

body:
## Summary

Items #4 and #5 of \`specs/SPEC_AGENT_PANE_FOLLOWUPS_2026_04_13.md\`, bundled since they share the same one-line rule and touch the same files.

## Item #4 — running/failed tools collapse to one line

**Before:** the \`running\` and \`failed\` states were **force-expanded**. Their content body rendered inline in the document flow, eating 2+ lines per tool even though the user's explicit rule is \"tools should be one line.\"

**After:** all statuses collapse by default. Hover reveals the body via the portal overlay (same path success tools already used after PR #367).

Progress + error information is still accessible:
- **Running:** ⏳ spinner in the summary, tool name visible, hover reveals the \"Running...\" body and any in-flight output.
- **Failed:** ✗ red status icon in the summary, tool name visible, hover reveals the full error payload.

Also simplifies the render: every expansion routes through the portal now, no more separate inline vs overlay branches. Removed the \`forceExpanded\` predicate entirely.

## Item #5 — error log lines collapse to one line

**Before:** \`.agent-status-line\` used \`white-space: pre-wrap\` — long error text wrapped into as many lines as it needed. A stack trace or a diagnostic blob could easily take 10–20 lines in the pane's log area.

**After:** CSS-only fix on \`.agent-status-line\`:
- \`white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis\` at rest.
- Hover expands to \`pre-wrap\`.
- Subtle background tint on hover so it's obvious the line is interactive.

Applies to all log line levels (info/warn/error), but the practical impact is on error/warn since those are the ones that wrap.

## Scope

**\`ToolBlock.tsx\`:**
- Drop \`forceExpanded\` accessor.
- \`expanded()\` = \`props.pinned || hovered()\` only.
- \`overlayMode()\` = \`hovered() || props.pinned\` (simplified — no more \`!forceExpanded\` guard).
- Drop the inline \`.agent-tool-content\` \`<Show>\` block — only the portal overlay renders expanded content now.

**\`agent-view.scss\`:**
- \`.agent-status-line\` → one-line clamp at rest, hover expands.

## Behavior change

- \`running\` / \`failed\` tools that were always showing their body are now collapsed until you hover.
- Long error log lines are one line until you hover.
- Success tools are unchanged (already collapsed since PR #346).
- Non-error log lines are unchanged behaviorally — they were already short enough to not wrap in practice.

## Test plan

- [x] \`task build:frontend\` clean
- [ ] Trigger a running tool → it shows one line with the ⏳ spinner, not a two-line block
- [ ] Hover the running tool → portal overlay expands with the 'Running...' body
- [ ] Trigger a failing tool (e.g. \`cat /nonexistent\`) → it shows one line with the ✗ icon
- [ ] Hover the failed tool → portal overlay shows the full error output
- [ ] Generate an error log line → appears as one line with ellipsis in the pane header
- [ ] Hover the error line → expands to show the full text
- [ ] Success tools unchanged

author: dacunni
body:
## Summary

- **Replace two-level binary search CDF with Walker alias table**: sampling goes from O(log w + log h) ≈ 20 iterations (with cache-unfriendly texture accesses) to O(1) — 2 array lookups + 1 comparison. The alias table is built once at load time from cosine-elevation-weighted pixel luminances, preserving the solid-angle-correct sampling distribution.
- **Eliminate coordinate round-trip in `sampleEnvironmentMap`**: the old path converted pixel (x,y) → trig → direction (`importanceSampleDirection`), then converted direction back → atan2/acos → bilinear lookup (`sampleRay`). The new `importanceSampleFull` returns direction + pdf + radiance together, fetching radiance directly from the texture at the already-known (x,y).
- **Memory**: roughly equivalent — `rowSums` (w×h texture) + `cumRows` (h-element vector) + `pdf2D` (w×h texture) replaced by `aliasProb` + `aliasIdx` (two flat w×h vectors) + one precomputed float `pdfNormFactor`. PDF convention is unchanged; renders are statistically identical.
- **Also**: propagated `sampleRay` `const`-correctness through all `EnvironmentMap` subclasses.

New virtual `EnvironmentMapSample importanceSampleFull(float e1, float e2) const` added to the base class with a default fallback. The existing `importanceSample` and `importanceSampleDirection` are preserved for backward compatibility (used by `tests/test_imp_samp_envmap.cpp`).

## Test plan

- [ ] All 19 unit tests pass (`ctest`)
- [ ] Visual inspection of a render using an HDR environment map — lighting should look the same as before
- [ ] Run `test_imp_samp_envmap` and verify sample distribution image looks correct (samples concentrated on bright regions)

## Summary
- Add two new CI workflows that run checks-qe scenarios in operator mode
- `e2e-checks-qe.yaml`: KinD cluster, runs on all PRs and nightly
- `e2e-checks-qe-ocp.yaml`: OCP 4.21 (CRC), upstream-only

## How it works

## Summary

Decomposes the only two remaining >100-line functions in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` so the file satisfies the <100-lines-per-function complexity threshold.

**`dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor`** (202 → 83 lines) — extracted into:
- `_dff_compute_capacity` — reads max workers, active workers, available slots
- `_dff_run_prepasses` — triage reviews + enrichment dispatch pre-passes
- `_dff_should_skip_candidate` — terminal blockers + fast-fail + empty body checks
- `_dff_process_candidate` — parse JSON, dispatch, verify launch, track round state
- `_dff_record_launch_failure` — canary cache invalidation on consecutive no-worker failures
- `_dff_maybe_engage_throttle` — post-round adaptive batch throttle decision

Round-state counters (`_DFF_ROUND_DISPATCHED`, `_DFF_ROUND_NO_WORKER_FAILURES`, `_DFF_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER`, `_DFF_THROTTLE_FILE`, `_DFF_CANARY_CACHE`, `_DFF_THROTTLE_CLEARED`) are module-level with a `_DFF_` prefix because bash 3.2 has no namerefs.

**`_run_preflight_stages`** (134 → 17 lines) — extracted into:
- `_preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` — cleanup stages + OpenCode DB archive + zombie reap + ledger expire
- `_preflight_capacity_and_labels` — calculate_max_workers + session count warn + needs-* label re-eval
- `_preflight_early_dispatch` — early fill floor + routine comment responses
- `_preflight_daily_scans` — complexity scan, CodeRabbit review, post-merge scanner, dedup cleanup, fast-fail prune
- `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` — contribution watch, normalize assignments, close merged, reconcile done, auto-approve
- `_preflight_prefetch_and_scope` — prefetch_state + PULSE_SCOPE_REPOS restore (returns 1 on abort)

Behavior is byte-for-byte equivalent to the pre-split code — every `run_stage_with_timeout` call, every log line, every error path is preserved. The decomposition is pure refactoring, no logic changes.

body:
## Summary
This PR performs a focused 4.3 balance pass for **Extra Events** with an emphasis on fixed-value rewards/costs and fleet-gate friction, while preserving the existing monthly-scaled reward system.

### What changed

- Rebalanced large **flat** resource constants (energy/unity/research) across key event chains to better fit 4.3 pacing.
- Kept `add_monthly_resource_mult` tier rewards broadly unchanged (by design), since they scale with current monthly income.
- Relaxed one fleet requirement that became harder to satisfy with 4.3’s fewer-but-stronger ships.
- Fixed one tier clamp inconsistency in a monthly-scaled reward.

## Key balance adjustments

### Flat energy/unity reductions (examples)
- `±2500` energy values reduced to `±1750` where used.
- `-2000` energy reduced to `-1400`.
- `500` energy rewards reduced to `350` (and `400` to `300` in one case).
- `±1000` unity values reduced to `±700`.
- `1500` unity reduced to `1000`.
- `800` unity reduced to `550`.
- `550/500/250` unity values in nomad-style options scaled down proportionally.

### Flat research lump-sum reductions (examples)
- `500` society research reduced to `300`.
- `300` society research reduced to `180`.
- `250` society research reduced to `150`.
- `200` society research reduced to `120`.

## Fleet / requirement compatibility

- Relaxed vortex project military requirement:
  - `shipclass_military = 2` -> `shipclass_military = 1`
  - File: `common/special_projects/eev_vortex_project.txt`

This keeps the branch reachable under 4.3 fleet composition realities without changing ship spawn counts.

## Tiered reward consistency fix

- Fixed `water_monster` tier bounds mismatch:
  - `value = @tier2unityreward` now correctly uses `min = @tier2unitymin` and `max = @tier2unitymax`
  - File: `events/eev_water_monster.txt`

author: oagr
body:
## Summary

Fixes QUA-419. `/sourcing/<type>/<id>` returned a raw Next.js 404 whenever the record had no `source_check_verdicts` row yet — which is the common case for wiki-pages (0% checked), investments (~74% unchecked), policy-stakeholders (~64%), and several other table types. Every dot click on an unchecked record was a dead end.

The record itself still exists in its source table (`/api/record-lookup/` returns 200 with full record data). Reuse that data to render a proper "not yet source-checked" empty state instead of 404.

## Fix

- New `UncheckedSourcingState` component (server-render, ~60 lines) with back link / type pill / title scaffolding, an explainer, and a link to the actual record.
- Page flow in `sourcing/[recordType]/[recordId]/page.tsx` now branches on the detail 404: if `recordResult.ok`, render the empty state; otherwise fall through to `notFound()` so genuinely-missing URLs still 404.

## Tests

- Unit tests for `UncheckedSourcingState` covering the with-link, no-link, and back-link render variants (4 passing).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run src/components/sourcing/UncheckedSourcingState.test.tsx` — 4 passing
- [ ] Manual: `/sourcing/wiki-page/<any-unchecked-id>` on prod after deploy → 200 with empty state
- [ ] Manual: `/sourcing/grant/garbage123xyz` → still 404
